policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Delhi Electric Vehicle Policy 2026 mandates that from Jan 1, 2027, only electric three-wheelers and light commercial vehicles can be registered in the national capital. From April 1, 2028, all new two-wheelers must also be electric.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Sweden has officially published a new law amending the Value Added Tax (VAT) Act. The measure is registered as Law No. SFS 2026:841. The new VAT rules will take effect on July 1, 2026, and apply only to taxable events occurring after that date.

From July 1st, a reduced Value Added Tax rate of 12 percent will be applied to sales of bread, milk, fresh poultry meat and eggs in Latvia. However, other meats (including all frozen and smoked meats plus sausages), bread snacks, cakes and buns, and other dairy products are not affected and will still have a 21 percent VAT rate applied to them.

Announced a temporary 135% customs duty on soft wheat o prioritize the marketing and industrial collection of the domestic harvest, which is projected to double to 9 million metric tons following the conclusion of a severe seven-year drought cycle. To ensure adequate supply-side stability, the state framework tied the tariff suspension to a domestic collection target of 80% of its 1.5 million ton soft wheat baseline by July 15, utilizing specialized handling and storage premiums for traders to counteract traditional farmer retention. Consequently, the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) forecasts Moroccan wheat imports to drop by 40% down to 4 million tons for the upcoming 2026/27 trading season. After the removal, the government will resume international imports and bolster national strategic stockpiles through January 2027. The temporary import tariff had been enacted from June 1 to July 31 t

Adopted stricter rules for steel imports to protect the European market from global overproduction and cheap competition, particularly from China, India, and Turkey. The new rules take effect on July 1. Under the new rules, the duty-free import quota will be limited to 18.3 million tons per year. Quantities exceeding this limit will be subject to a punitive tariff of 50 percent, twice as much as before.

The Reserve Bank of India has issued the Amendment Directions under the Reserve Bank of India (Commercial Banks Credit Facilities) Directions, 2026 (Revised) dated 30 March 2026. The Directions will take effect on 1 July 2026. They have introduced a structured framework for commercial bank financing of corporate acquisitions, a type of commercial lending that had only been given a few carve-outs in the regulatory framework. The Directions also restated the regime relating to loans against financial assets and add a new chapter on credit to capital market intermediaries.

From 1 July 2026, the EU will apply a temporary €3 customs duty per item on low-value consignments (up to €150) imported from outside the EU, abolishing the duty exemption applicable until 30 June 2026. The €3 temporary customs duty is a flat fee, which will apply until 1 July 2028, after which normal customs duties will apply, depending on the type of good.
Consumers in Cyprus ordering goods from outside the European Union will begin paying a temporary EUR 3 customs duty per product category from July 1, 2026.

Sigend a decree to increase the amount of salaries, pensions, stipends and allowances (No. PF-115), providing for an increase in social payments, salaries of public sector employees and stipends. The amounts of pensions and allowances, including child allowances and material assistance to families included in the "Social Register", will be increased by 7 percent.

country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
policydecision_details: The United Kingdom government will implement a new steel trade measure effective from 1 July 2026, which limits tariff-free steel imports by reducing overall quota volumes by 51 percent compared to the previous safeguard measure. Imports exceeding these established quarterly quotas will be subject to a 50 percent tariff, while the existing 25 percent safeguard duty will cease to apply after 30 June 2026. Administered by HM Revenue and Customs on a first come, first served basis, this policy applies to steel products that can be manufactured domestically, with specific exemptions for goods originating in Ukraine and a time-limited transitional arrangement for contracts signed before 14 March 2026.
Announced that from July 1, 2026, franchise AP holders may import only completely built‑up (CBU) electric vehicles, aiming to encourage greater localisation in mass‑market segments.
Issued the Decree 161/2026/ND-CP base salary and bonus regime for cadres, civil servants, public employees, armed forces. From July 01, 2026, the base salary is VND 2,530,000/month (usd100).

The first Vietnam Grand Sale in 2026 will take place from July 1-31 nationwide. The annual event is expected to attract broad participation from businesses across sectors through traditional trade promotion activities and e-commerce initiatives.

Advanced its comprehensive national livestock vaccination and tagging campaign across the high-priority pastoral zones of Masafer Yatta and the northern Jordan Valley. Operating through localized veterinary teams and the Tubas Directorate of Agriculture and Veterinary Services, the targeted public health intervention completed field operations across the communities of Zuweidin, Umm Qussa, Umm al-Khair, al-Kharba, Khirbet Ibziq, and the Tubas Plain. During this specific deployment phase, field teams administered preventative vaccinations against the foot-and-mouth disease (SAT-1) strain to 2,950 sheep and integrated 3,320 sheep into the national electronic tagging and traceability system, directly supporting 53 localized livestock breeders. By scaling the cumulative campaign total to more than 43,620 head of livestock, the state-backed sanitary program is engineered to reduce the transmission of trans-boundary animal epidemics, build smallholder climate and economic resilience, and strengthen macro-level national herd tracking and food security infrastructure.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Delhi government has approved an ambitious electric vehicle (EV) policy. The new policy also offers a 1 lakh rupees incentive for purchasing new EVs while scrapping old vehicles, and mandates that only electric two-wheelers can be registered starting April 2028. Set for a phased four-year rollout starting from 1st of July, the ambitious framework commits a massive fiscal outlay of 15 thousand crore rupees to completely transition the national capital toward zero-emission transit by 31st March 2030.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Announced an expansion of the New Industry Brazil (NIB) program, making an additional BRL 140 billion (USD 25.4 billion) available for investment. Unlike industrial strategies adopted in previous decades, the federal government argues that the effectiveness of the new industrial policy should not be measured by an increase in the manufacturing sector's share of Gross Domestic Product (GDP), a shift that, according to its architects, may not necessarily occur in the short term.
The French parliament passed a bill aimed at curbing the rise of fast fashion, targeting major Asian e-commerce platforms.

Instituted an exceptional logistical and digital framework to streamline national harvesting operations and secure seasonal cereal yields. Central to this initiative is the deployment of the digital platform hassad.dz, which enables farmers to electronically request combine harvesters and declare production volumes. To eliminate administrative bottlenecks during this record production season, the ministry has bypassed traditional requirements by allowing unregistered producers without a formal farmer's card to deliver their yields directly to the Cereal and Pulses Cooperatives (CCLS) upon registration via the portal. Backed by a joint machinery agreement between PMAT Trading and AGRODRIVE, the Algerian Interprofessional Cereals Office (OAIC) has mobilized a specialized fleet of more than 1,300 combine harvesters to fill regional equipment deficits. Furthermore, the state has ordered all localized storage centers and strategic silos—recently expanded under national infrastructure programs—to operate continuously seven days a week with extended working hours, including weekends and public holidays. This comprehensive public intervention is engineered to eliminate field queues, maximize transport logistics, and enhance national food sovereignty through real-time agrifood asset management.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Launched a state-backed climate adaptation initiative titled "From Scarcity to Sustainability: Building Adaptive Drought Interventions in Agriculture." Financed by the Government of Japan, the targeted project scales agroecological and climate-smart agricultural frameworks across vulnerable, drought-prone, and refugee-hosting communities within northern regions, specifically targeting approximately 380 beneficiaries across Ajloun, Jerash, and Northern Shuna. By establishing strategic demonstration sites, distributing modern agricultural inputs, and upgrading institutional capacities in water resource management and drought preparedness, the joint framework is engineered to optimize resource efficiency, safeguard smallholder and women-led cooperative livelihoods, and reinforce macro-level national food security baselines.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Launched the "My Water (Maee)" Award during the inaugural Saudi Water Week in Jeddah. Designed as a key strategic initiative to incentivize national sustainability goals, the award framework establishes a competitive national environment to stimulate scientific innovation, promote cross-sector efficiency benchmarks, and recognize outstanding engineering and conservation practices across public, private, and civil sectors. By embedding the launch within a high-level international utility summit, the state-backed center aims to accelerate the adoption of high-impact water-use technologies, cultivate a culture of resource stewardship, and preserve critical water reserves for future generations.
Abandoned its 15-year dollar peg and moved to a flexible exchange rate, with the boliviano depreciating roughly 30 percent to around 9.73 per dollar as La Paz pursues an IMF financing deal.

Expanded its national livestock vaccination and tagging campaign into its second consecutive week, scaling total coverage to more than 30,700 head of livestock since launch. Designed as a localized veterinary public health framework to insulate smallholder herds against epidemic threats like foot-and-mouth disease (SAT-1), the field initiative deployed specialized mobile teams to execute targeted treatments, including vaccinating and tagging 2,000 head across the Umm Qussa and Zuweidin communities in Masafer Yatta, alongside an additional 1,100 head within the Ibziq and Bardala areas of the Tubas and Northern Jordan Valley Governorate. By integrating preventative immunological controls with a standardized digital identification system to enhance animal health tracking and biosecurity governance, this state-backed program directly mitigates transboundary disease vectors, safeguards domestic livestock assets, and bolsters the economic resilience of vulnerable rural farming families.

Approved new financing allocations totaling EGP 499.415 million (USD 10.1 million) under the National Veal Project, expanding targeted smallholder credit lines to 372 additional beneficiaries, including small-scale breeders and young graduates. Integrated within the framework of the presidential "Decent Life" (Haya Karima) rural development initiative, the latest state-backed funding tier will finance the procurement and intensive fattening of 7,137 head of livestock. Backed by joint credit disbursements from the Agricultural Bank of Egypt and the National Bank of Egypt, alongside subsidized coverage from the Livestock Insurance Fund, the national program has scaled its cumulative portfolio to EGP 11.172 billion (USD 226 million), directly modernizing livestock infrastructure for over 46,000 breeders managing more than 538,500 head of cattle. Through intensified veterinary field monitoring and technical oversight from the Livestock and Poultry Development Sector, this public-private framework is engineered to compress the national red meat and dairy food gap, stabilize volatile domestic primary commodity prices, and increase rural household incomes.

Expanded operations at the Mango Gene Bank within the Sohar Agricultural Research Station, establishing one of the largest field genetic repositories for the crop in the region. Designed as a living database and a strategic buffer against climate-induced agricultural pressures, the research center houses 252 local and international mango varieties distributed across 708 trees—including 62 distinct Omani cultivars collected across various governorates and specimens from 23 leading fruit-producing nations. By deploying advanced phenotypic profiling, genetic fingerprinting, and artificial intelligence models, state researchers isolate high-yield genetic traits to breed new, resilient cultivars optimized for drought tolerance, extreme heat, and salinity resistance. This public-sector biotechnology initiative is engineered to optimize domestic nursery pipelines, supply commercial farmers with premium propagation materials, and eliminate international seedling dependency, directly strengthening Oman's long-term food security and agricultural export competitiveness

Completed the handover of the first phase of a specialized infrastructure modernization project across fish landing centers in Hodeida governorate. Financed through a state-backed allocation of 93 million Yemeni rials, the initial phase establishes eight fully equipped, prefabricated administrative service centers out of a planned 14-center network designed to streamline local maritime governance. Formally launched by the Hodeida local authority leadership, the regulatory infrastructure framework is engineered to optimize fish catch data collection, issue fishing vessel licenses, and standardize transit permits for marketing vehicles, directly safeguarding product quality from coastal landing points to retail markets. By upgrading these crucial logistical nodes, the public sector initiative reinforces regional food security, safeguards marine resources, and supports localized economic development for thousands of smallholder artisanal fishing families along the Red Sea coast.

Declared a 90-days state of emergency. The measure allows for military intervention and the suspension of some individual rights, giving the government a narrow window to push through economic measures aimed at stabilizing the country and restoring investor confidence.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Announced a 22.5 MW solar plant project as part of its strategy to achieve 30 percent renewable energy generation by 2030. This initiative reflects ongoing efforts to address rising fuel costs and environmental concerns within the country.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Restructured its fiscal policy governing agricultural inputs by replacing the fixed USD 90 per metric tonne nitrogen fertilizer export levy with a flexible 10 percent duty calculated on the free-on-board (FOB) invoice value of each shipment. Formally enacted via publication in the Official Gazette, the revised tax framework is engineered to align state export revenues directly with fluctuating global market values while providing domestic exporters with greater financial flexibility during periods of international price deflations. To incentivize specialized industrial activity and safeguard regional trade corridors, the policy completely exempts high-grade pure ammonium nitrate exceeding a 34.2 percent nitrogen threshold, alongside shipments allocated to productive enterprises operating within Egypt’s designated free zones. This state-backed fiscal adjustment carries significant weight for international supply chains, as market forecasts predict heightened price volatility due to ongoing maritime shipping risks around the Strait of Hormuz, maintaining Egypt's strategic position as the world’s seventh-largest exporter of nitrogen fertilizers.

Launched the sixth consecutive annual national wheat purchase campaign to collect and process the 2026 domestic grain harvest from smallholders across several governorates. Engineered as a state-backed agrifood localization framework, the procurement initiative establishes an organized, reliable wholesale marketing channel that provides local farmers with fair, stabilized pricing, encouraging the expansion of cultivated acreage and the deployment of modern farming technologies. By integrating the harvested crop directly into domestic processing facilities to manufacture Oman-made food products, the public-private partnership effectively closes the agricultural value chain, optimizes local value addition (ICV), and minimizes international grain import reliance in alignment with national food security strategy objectives.

Formalized a joint technical document to enhance transboundary cooperation and data exchange regarding shared water assets, with particular emphasis on the Euphrates River basin. Co-chaired by technical undersecretaries and ministerial delegations from both nations, the bilateral session established updated coordination mechanisms and direct channels for exchanging field information and hydrometric data. Convened under the strategic guidance of the Iraqi water resources ministry, the collaborative framework seeks to institutionalize risk-based water resource management, optimize seasonal river flow allocations, and deploy technical early warning channels to mitigate regional drought and flood vulnerabilities.

Structured a major public-private investment opportunity to construct the Al Salil Smart Agricultural Cluster in Quriyat, a specialized agrotech development requiring a capital expenditure of OMR 17 million (USD 44.2 million). Spanning over 2.09 million square meters, the mega-cluster is engineered to consolidate multi-tiered farming operations combining open-field plots, shade-net facilities, climate-controlled smart greenhouses, and yield-intensive vertical farming systems to generate an estimated 62 million kilograms of annual crop output, targeting high-value commodities such as strawberries, cherry tomatoes, and water-efficient leafy greens. Utilizing optimized irrigation networks drawing from the Wadi Dayqah Dam and regional groundwater reserves, the phased infrastructure project is strategically positioned near the Muscat consumer market to scale up national fruit and vegetable self-sufficiency, generate rural technical employment, and significantly lower the country's international food import bill.

Planned to shift from in-kind food subsidies to a cash-based or cash-valued support system in fiscal year 2026/2027, with the reform expected to be introduced gradually and Port Said likely to serve as the first pilot governorate before any nationwide rollout.

Released two new guides to help Brazilian companies take advantage of opportunities created by the Mercosur-European Union agreement. The guides cover rules of origin and geographical indications, two key areas for exporters, producers, foreign trade operators and other companies seeking to access the benefits of the agreement.

Inspected 255 hectares of Jatropha curcas in the department of Atlántico, Colombia, as part of the Good Agricultural Practices certification process for Empresa Agroforestal de Colombia S.A.S. The project is distributed across three farms in the municipalities of Piojó and Ponedera and aims to produce sustainable vegetable oil for international markets, including China. At peak productivity, the harvest can reach up to 5 tonnes of fruit per hectare per year, generating between 550 and 600 liters of oil per hectare.

Cancelled approximately USD 10.8 million that had been allocated to the Rural Insurance Premium Subsidy Program. The reduction follows an approximately USD 89 million budget freeze in May and a previous USD 5 million cancellation, out of an initial budget of approximately USD 194.6 million set in the 2026 Annual Budget Law.

Published Legislative Decree No. 146/2026 , approving the Free Trade Agreement between Mercosur and EFTA (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, and Switzerland). The agreement provides for the liberalization of approximately 97 percent of bilateral trade and the gradual reduction of tariffs to 1.2%, with preferential access to nearly 99 percent of Brazilian exports. Upon entry into force, the agreement will eliminate tariffs on industrial and fishing products from EFTA countries, directly impacting the competitiveness of Brazilian industry. In the agricultural sector, the agreement combines tariff reductions with quotas for items such as meat, corn, honey, and vegetable oils.

Launched a programme to help family farms and small businesses enter international markets. The programme is currently being expanded, with plans to cover 450 cooperatives by the end of 2026. Of these, 200 will receive training and preparation to enter export markets, whilst a further 250 will be able to take part in international exhibitions, trade missions and negotiations with potential partners.

Approved new national Foot-and-Mouth Disease (FMD) control measures that will provide farmers, veterinarians and veterinary authorities with a clear, practical and science-based framework for managing outbreaks while minimising unnecessary economic losses. The measures consolidate and replace previous directives issued under Section 9 of the Animal Diseases Act, including the 2019 FMD Contingency Plan, subsequent amendments and related protocols. For the first time, South Africa will have a single, integrated set of national control measures that clearly outline how outbreaks must be managed from detection through to recovery.

Required food importers to source at least 20 planned of planned import volumes from domestic producers before obtaining or renewing import licenses. The measure extends the government's long-running import substitution strategy aimed at strengthening local agriculture and reducing dependence on foreign food supplies.

Approved the Personal Income Tax Code Law, which aims to ensure greater security in addressing practices that may constitute money laundering offenses, as well as to strengthen mechanisms for identifying, assessing, and mitigating underlying risk factors. Among the measures envisaged are exemptions for earned income received by people with a disability rating of 50% or higher, as well as for the income of strategic personnel assigned to diplomatic and consular missions. It also provides for exemptions for income earned by people with a disability rating of 50% or higher and for the income of strategic personnel at diplomatic and consular missions.

The government will increase compensation for farmers affected by attacks by the Iberian wolf, the minister of cabinet affairs announced, explaining that the aim is to redress the balance for farmers while protecting the species.

The Luxembourg government has taken a significant step by enshrining the right to be forgotten in law, following in the footsteps of other European countries. This measure aims to make it easier for people who have recovered from serious illnesses to access credit and insurance.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: Approved a series of fiscal measures to support regional development and the agro-industrial complex. These include writing off nearly 50 billion roubles (USD 649 million) in federal budget obligations for eight regions (the Udmurt Republic and the Volgograd, Moscow, Nizhny Novgorod, Novgorod, Novosibirsk, Ryazan, and Chelyabinsk regions) to fund infrastructure and housing projects, alongside allocating approximately 60 billion roubles (USD 779 million) in subsidies to support over 41,000 agricultural loans. Additionally, 2.5 billion roubles (USD 32 million) have been designated for flood prevention in the North Caucasus, and over 6.5 billion roubles (USD 84 million) for social payments in the Donbass and Novorossiya regions, as well as funds for utility equipment in these areas. These coordinated actions are aimed at ensuring economic growth, food security, and improved living standards across the country.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: Released temporary relief from the to commercial banks, a move meant to keep market volatility from squeezing capital ratios.
Announced additional financing support for exporters to maintain the momentum in foreign sales and reach USD 50 billion in exports to distant markets by 2028.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The Hungarian government has ordered a coordinated nationwide response to the ongoing heatwave.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The European Commission approved on Friday, June 26, a state-ensured capital increase of EUR 1 billion and the extension of the state guarantee granted to the Investment and Development Bank until the end of 2032 for Romania.
Issued a notification classifiying cannabis inflorescence as a controlled herb. From that date, GACP supply chain traceability became a condition of the export license.
The Dutch cabinet has finalised agreement on a new package of measures to reduce nitrogen-based pollution in the Netherlands with a budget of EUR 20 billion to implement them.

Construction has commenced on the Kazarman hydropower cascade in the Jalal-Abad region of Kyrgyzstan. The new hydroelectric complex, located in the Toguz-Toro district, is estimated to cost approximately USD 3 billion.

Agreement between Japan and the Kyrgyz Republic for the Elimination of Double Taxation with respect to Taxes on Income and the Prevention of Tax Evasion and Avoidance” (signed on December 19, 2025) were completed between the Government of Japan and the Government of the Kyrgyz Republic.

Introduced the Home Market Restoration Act of 2026, legislation to establish tariff-rate quotas (TRQs) on shrimp and a number of import-sensitive food and agricultural products. The bill aims to stop import surges and restore fair prices to support U.S. food producers, while allowing lawful trade.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Approved a series of measures aimed at strengthening regional integration, expanding trade, modernizing financial legislation and advancing the country’s energy sector.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Launched the Agricultural Value Chain Development Project to develop the eastern region and increase agricultural productivity, with a focus on rice and poultry farming, involving an investment of USD 210 million within 5 years. It is expected to benefit 240,000 people directly—50 percent of whom are women and 60% young people—as well as small-scale producers, with special attention given to agro-pastoral communities, people with disabilities, former military personnel, and widows. The project includes a USD 190 million loan from the African Development Bank (AfDB) toward the total investment.

Announced a memorandum of understanding to advance the use of biobanking and genomic science in support of wildlife conservation and species recovery. The agreement establishes a framework for partnership focused on preserving genetic diversity among threatened and endangered species, expanding scientific understanding of genomic applications in conservation, and exploring emerging technologies that may strengthen recovery efforts for species at risk.

Finalized a EUR 123 million integrated municipal infrastructure package to expand the Madaba wastewater treatment plant and scale up regional sewage networks. Funded via a EUR 25 million European Union grant channelled through the AFD, alongside EUR 97 million in joint credit facilities from the AFD and KfW, the three-year environmental engineering initiative will construct a new treatment facility boosting the governorate's capacity to 16,000 cubic meters per day to serve approximately 200,000 residents. Managed locally by the Madaba Water Administration, the structural climate-adaptation framework incorporates the installation of dedicated transmission pipelines to route reclaimed, treated wastewater exclusively toward restricted agricultural sectors, optimizing non-conventional water utilities while alleviating compounding resource pressures on natural fresh irrigation supplies.

Banned the importation of bioethanol feedstock, including molasses and other sugar products. The order also stated that any approval for importation of feedstock must be authorized by the National Biofuels Board (NBB). The SRA said that allowing imports of sugar products for bioethanol production conflicts with the mandates of Republic Act (RA) 9367 or the Biofuels Act.
Issued a decision requiring insurance companies to comply with a set of regulatory standards governing reinsurance operations.
Announced the extension of the exemptions on environmental protection tax, VAT and most-favored nation import duty on petroleum products for additional three months.

Greece's Environment and Energy Ministry has launched an emergency EUR 15 million (USD 17 million) programme to combat severe water shortages across nine island municipalities, as intensifying summer droughts strain local supplies during the peak tourist season.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The German coalition government has adopted a draft law reform to ease requirements on businesses to become more energy efficient, including data centres. Germany’s industry welcomed the proposed changes as a step in the right direction of cutting bureaucracy, but other stakeholders are more critical about what they see as a weakening of energy efficiency rules needed to achieve climate neutrality.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The European Commission has approved an EUR 8 million(USD 9 million) Croatian state aid scheme to support fishing companies facing higher fuel prices linked to the Middle East crisis.

The EU Council gave final approval to the bloc's tariff commitments under its trade framework with the US, clearing the way for the deal to enter into force. In a statement, the council said member states formally adopted the two regulations linked to the EU-US Joint Statement of Aug. 21, 2025, completing the bloc's legislative process. Under the measures, the EU will eliminate remaining customs duties on US industrial goods and provide preferential market access for certain US seafood and non-sensitive agricultural products.

Cyprus motorists will continue to benefit from lower fuel taxes for at least another two months, after Parliament unanimously approved an emergency bill extending the government's fuel tax relief measure.

Supported 400 workers from India and Bangladesh, by giving each worker SGD 100 (USD 78) in cash and SGD 100 (USD 78) in FairPrice supermarket vouchers to help meet daily expenses. The NTUC has also identified 150 construction job vacancies from around 40 employers over the past two days.

Decided to reduce import duties under the proposed National Tariff Policy 2025–30 to lower trade costs, boost economic activity, and make the market more competitive. The five-year policy proposes phased cuts to customs duties, regulatory duties, and additional customs duties, with the overall average tariff targeted to fall from 20.19 percent to 9.70 percent. The reforms are expected to reduce government revenue by an estimated PKR 143 billion (approximately USD 503 million), but lower tariffs are expected to encourage trade, reduce import costs, and improve competition across multiple sectors.

Signed three cooperation agreements with Türkiye to get support for the privatization of electricity and power sector. The agreements include a cooperation protocol between Turkish Electricity Distribution Company (TEDAS) and Pakistan Power Planning and Monitoring Company (PPMC) to strengthen operational monitoring of distribution companies and establish virtual reality-based training centers.
Increased the amount of US dollars issued to banks by 25 percent during the tourist off season, in a move aimed at easing pressure in the foreign exchange market.
Passed new commodity exchange law introducing stricter institutional standards.

Ratified an economic partnership agreement betwen the UAE and the EAEU. One of the key provisions of the document is the elimination of customs duties on a range of goods, as well as the simplification of market access for products from both sides. The Kyrgyz government notes that the implementation of the agreement will enable domestic exporters to supply the UAE market, duty-free, with a range of goods of vital importance to the country’s economy, including mutton, beef, tinned meat and offal, honey, nuts, dried vegetables, fruit juices, and fermented milk products.

Announced an increase of domestically produced construction materials in large-scale infrastructure and tourism project, while supporting local manufacturers through new policy measures and targeted financial assistance.

Formally adopted two regulations implementing the tariff commitments set out in the EU-US Declaration of 21 August 2025. This adoption completes the legislative process and confirms the EU’s commitment to a stable, predictable and mutually beneficial transatlantic trade relationship, whilst preserving the necessary safeguards to protect European economic interests. The two regulations remove the remaining EU tariffs on US industrial products, introduce preferential access for certain non-sensitive US fishery and agricultural products through tariff quotas and reduced tariffs, and extend the suspension of tariffs on imports of lobsters, including processed lobsters (from all countries on the basis of the most-favoured-nation principle). The regulations also contain strengthened safeguard and suspension mechanisms.

The Government today approved the launch of negotiations and the signing of the Financing Contract between the Republic of Moldova and the European Investment Bank for the implementation of Livada Moldovei II project. The project envisages contracting a loan of EUR 150 million (USD 171 million), on favorable terms, intended for the modernization and strengthening of the agri-food sector.
The programme, announced by Finance Minister will provide a basic quota of 200 litres of subsidised diesel at RM2.10 per litre.

Distributed 130 tons of barley fodder to 463 sheep farmers across the western communities of Dura, including Al-Burj, Beit Marsam, Al-Bireh, and surrounding villages. Executed as part of the Emergency Humanitarian Assistance Project with structural financial support from Italian Cooperation, the emergency logistics deployment provides vital nutritional inputs to safeguard livestock herds and insulate smallholders from compounding operational overheads. By stabilizing feed availability for vulnerable livestock breeders amidst severe regional economic disruptions, the inter-institutional intervention mitigates flock mortality risks, sustains domestic meat and dairy production capabilities, and directly reinforces baseline household food security.

Passed amendments to the Tax Code aimed at addressing domestic fuel shortages, which have been exacerbated by Ukrainian drone strikes on refineries. The measures include allowing the blending of lower-quality fuel, delaying refinery equipment upgrades, and introducing import subsidies linked to Indian delivery costs and prices, while the government is also considering a diesel export ban.

Passed a bill freezing the VAT exemption threshold for small businesses using the simplified tax system at 20 million rubles (USD 260,000) through 2029, reversing a previously scheduled gradual reduction. Under the new timeline, the threshold will decrease to 15 million rubles (USD 195,000) in 2029 and to 10 million rubles (USD 130,000) in 2030. However, the relief does not extend to patent-system businesses, prompting business lobby groups to call for broader coverage of the measure.

The Greek government recently announced a new National Organization for Cadastre and Building Control, a centralized body intended to streamline Greece’s property, planning and building permit procedures through a unified digital platform. Government officials said the Land Registry is expected to move fully into operational mode by the end of 2026, providing a nationwide digital record of property ownership and land information.

policy_description: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
policydecision_details: The European Commission published a Regulation imposing definitive anti-dumping duties on imports of 1,4-Butanediol (‘BDO’) originating in the People’s Republic of China, Saudi Arabia and the United States of America.
policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures

policydecision_details: On 24 June 2026, the European Commission adopted an ambitious tax simplification package that includes two legislative proposals aimed at simplifying EU tax rules, reducing compliance burdens for businesses, and strengthening the competitiveness of the Internal Market. The direct taxation Omnibus and the Recast of the Directive on Administrative Cooperation (DAC) are designed to modernise the EU's direct tax framework, make it more efficient and better adapt it to the current economic environment, while maintaining the same level of strong protection against tax fraud, avoidance and evasion.

Planned to gradually reduce import tax burdens and reorganize the tariff structure in the next five years. Specifically, these include: gradually eliminating Additional Customs Duty (ACD) in the next five years; gradually reducing Regulatory Duty and eventually reducing it to zero; controlling the maximum rate of ordinary tariffs within 15 percent; controlling the maximum rate of regulatory taxes within 20 percent; abolishing low-end regulatory tax rates such as 1 percent, 2 percent, and 2.5 percent.

policy_description: Unspecified genetic resources and sanitary measures
policydecision_details: Approved agricultural biotechnology policy to provide a framework for biotechnology research, product commercialisation, crop productivity and food and nutrition security. Under NABP-2025, agricultural biotechnology has been divided into regulated and non-regulated areas. The regulated areas include the development and commercialisation of genetically modified organisms, gene editing, import and export of GM products, and recombinant vaccines for animals.
policycategory: Unspecified genetic resources and sanitary measures

policydecision_details: Launched a PKR 1.58 billion (USD 5.6 million) School Meal Program for primary school students in Balochistan, aiming to improve child nutrition, health, school attendance, and classroom learning. The project will start as a pilot, with PKR 315.9 million (USD 1.1 million) allocated for the current year.

Imposed a six-month ban on coal exports by road. The temporary ban applies to coal from Kyrgyzstan classified under HS codes 2701 and 2702, an official document shows. But the ban will not apply to shipments through the Irkeshtam and Torugart border crossings.
Distributed a salary for citizens who participate in the elections, as the election day has been declared a non-working day.

Approved to maintain its policy rate at 1.00 percent. The decision was driven by economic growth that, while stronger than previously assessed, remains low and uneven, particularly impacting SMEs and households. Inflation is expected to rise temporarily due to supply-side factors before easing, but the committee views the current accommodative policy as appropriate to support the recovery. The committee noted that overall credit growth is low, and the loan quality of SMEs and vulnerable households requires monitoring.
Announced it will extend its preferential tariff on Taiwanese exports of banana, pineapples and mangoes.
Issued Resolution No. 919 temporarily establishing an import-tariff rate quota for medicaments containing fluor.

Received approval for a 36-month precautionary Stand-By Arrangement from the IMF worth SDR 189 million (USD 259 million)—equivalent to 200 percent of Barbados’s quota in the Fund—and concluded its 2026 Article IV review of the economy.
Formally issued a wide-ranging license permitting the sale of Iranian oil for 60 days.

Received the approval for a USD 150 million financing package from IDB to support improvements in water security, drinking water and sanitation services, and agricultural productivity in the Argentine province of Mendoza. The initiative is expected to benefit more than 1.6 million people through both direct and indirect impacts. The programme aims to increase the availability and quality of water resources by upgrading wastewater treatment infrastructure and reinforcing water resource management systems, which play a key role in Mendoza’s economy.

Validated national AfCFTA strategy and action plan. The plan is a diversification play for an economy in which crude still accounts for roughly 95 percent of goods exports. The plan’s stated priorities, as set out by the organizers, are to strengthen domestic productive capacity, build regional value chains, push more local firms into regional markets, and steer benefits toward women, youth and other vulnerable groups. Bineswaree Bolaky, the ECA economic affairs officer who coordinated the support, argued that the private sector should be “the main beneficiary and the main driver” of the process, contingent on an enabling business environment and responsive state institutions — a pointed framing in a country where the state and the oil sector have long dominated economic life.

Kazakhstan has introduced a temporary ban on imports of fresh and chilled tomatoes from non-EAEU countries. The measure took effect on 22 June following an order signed by the Minister of Agriculture. The restrictions will remain in force until 30 June 2026. The ban applies to tomato imports by all modes of transport.

Officially initiated its sixth consecutive national wheat procurement and purchase program for the 2026 harvest season. Designed as a key agricultural localization and smallholder empowerment initiative under the overarching framework of the Oman Vision 2040 development strategy, the program provides Omani farmers across multiple governorates with an organized, guaranteed marketing channel and standardized technical benchmarks for grain supply. By receiving, processing, and converting diverse domestic wheat varieties into added-value national food products, the enterprise has successfully accelerated local wheat output nearly 20-fold since 2021, thereby expanding strategic domestic grain reserves from an eight-month to a ten-month supply, reducing import dependency risks, and safeguarding localized rural livelihoods.

Authorized the allocation of JOD 169,342 (USD 239,000) from the Jordan–Japan Counterpart Fund to finance the construction of localized water harvesting infrastructure in Wadi Araba, within the Aqaba Governorate, to support the Jordan Valley Authority.

Supervised and executed a targeted agricultural input deployment to distribute 18,300 summer vegetable seedlings to 61 smallholder beneficiaries with home gardens across Al-Karmel, Al-Riha, As-Samu, and Yatta. Implemented under the framework of the "Nutrition and Care of Palestinian Children through Agriculture" project in partnership with Diakonia and Radio Hellen, the intervention allocates 300 assorted seedlings to each household. By providing vulnerable families with the necessary material inputs and direct technical guidance to optimize home-based crop cultivation, the structural program aims to scale up localized micro-agricultural production, reduce household food expenditure, and elevate baseline nutritional security for children and women in rural communities.

Completed its domestic approval process for a digital economy partnership agreement among members of the Organization of Turkic States (OTS), bringing the bloc closer to a new framework for digital trade and economic integration. The deal will enter into force after Kyrgyzstan and Kazakhstan also complete their domestic approval procedures.
Appointed a special panel to protect lands in Eastern Province with an aim to stop illegal land grabbing and promote tourism while repossessing unutilized government lands, the government said.

Appointed a 15-member Public Servants’ Salaries and Pensions Commission to examine long-standing salary and pension-related issues affecting public officers and pensioners, and to recommend reforms aimed at strengthening Sri Lanka’s public service.
Decided not to implement a key Value Added Tax (VAT) reform announced in the 2026 Budget.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Kazakhstan, Trinidad and Tobago and Chad will receive some funding from the $20mn Beyond Oil and Gas Alliance (Boga) fund, to support development of plans to transition away from fossil fuels.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policy_description: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
policydecision_details: The Japanese Government has announced plans to impose anti-dumping duties on imports of nickel-containing cold-rolled stainless steel from China and Taiwan. The reason for this decision was a policy of unfair pricing, which has caused significant damage to Japanese manufacturers.
policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures

policydecision_details: The Indonesian Government will disburse a IDR 26.34 trillion (USD 1.48 billion) economic stimulus package in the second half of 2026 to support growth, boost consumption and strengthen social welfare.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: European Commission to mobilise over EUR 56 million (USD 64.1 million) from the agricultural reserve. Farmers from Portugal will receive USD 34 million, Romania USD 17 million, Cyprus €4.6 million, Croatia USD 5 million, and Slovenia USD 3 million. These funds will support farmers affected by significant damage from adverse climatic events. The support will be directed at fruit, nut, vine, olive and arable crop farmers, including mixed livestock producers.The allocated budgetcan be complemented by up to 200% of national funds.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Unveiled the coastal defence rules, requiring long-term protection against rising seas. According to the new rules, landowners with 30 years or more remaining on leases must plan for a potential 2.15-metre sea level rise by 2150 under worst-case climate scenarios.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Received the approval for a policy-loan from Asia Development Bank of USD 700 million for a program that supports the transformation of insurance sector from a legacy, rules-based framework to a modern, risk-based, and market-oriented system. The reforms will help mobilize patient capital for development, expand financial protection for households and businesses, and support a more competitive, inclusive, and resilient insurance market.
Announced moves to curb the rapid growth of buy-now-pay-later services.
Launched a national public education campaign aimed at fostering greater understanding and discussion surrounding the implementation of Maya customary land rights in Belize.
The Ministry of Health today unveiled the “Guidelines on Healthy School Canteens”, aimed at creating student‑friendly canteens that provide affordable, safe, and nutritious meals.

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations
policydecision_details: The Norwegian government has announced new classifications for the country's 13 salmon farming regions under its "traffic light" system, designed to regulate production based on the environmental impact of salmon lice on wild salmon populations.
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: The Selangor government has allocated RM1.5 million for the Selangor Career Programme to accelerate job-matching initiatives and help those who have lost their jobs find new career opportunitie

Kazakhstan will abolish the rule requiring adjustment of input VAT amounts for agricultural product exporters. The decision was made during a meeting of the Project Office for the implementation of the new Tax Code, chaired by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy.

Launched a digital platform enabling the electronic submission of sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) documentation for agrifood imports. Executed as a core milestone under Morocco’s 2025–2027 Foreign Trade Roadmap, the real-time interoperability between both organizations' information systems eliminates manual data redundancies and accelerates the validation of Single Goods Declarations (DUM). By digitalizing the complex regulatory compliance checks required for agricultural imports, the initiative aims to slash transit bottlenecks at maritime ports and airports, enhance national logistics competitiveness, and minimize the time perishable products spend in transit undergoing necessary health and safety controls.

Expanded its advanced diagnostic and laboratory testing services to enhance animal health and support livestock breeders. Managed by the Central Veterinary Laboratories and Research Department, technical teams utilize modern technologies to facilitate early disease detection and improve veterinary care efficiency. Recent diagnostics include 385 ELISA serological tests, 159 bacteriological examinations, 49 poultry disease assessments, and 145 public health and food safety evaluations. These targeted epidemiological and diagnostic efforts are designed to safeguard livestock production quality, minimize economic losses for breeders, and bolster national food security

Introduced an 8% export duty on rough diamonds weighing between 0.45 and 10.8 carats, as well as on special-size stones over 10.8 carats, effective September 1, 2026, with the aim of supporting the domestic diamond cutting industry. The duty reverses a 2016 WTO-driven removal of such tariffs and is designed to apply only to stones that are economically viable to cut within Russia.

Handed out almost two-thirds of the NIS 3 billion they committed to transfer to the public through benefits, within two years. This is part of a voluntary plan adopted in April 2025 by the banks to help customers in an era of high interest rates, and high profits for the banks.

Unveiled seven strategies and action plans for the Indonesian Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (IBSAP) 2025-2045. Jumhur said the action plan is aligned with the country's long-term and medium-term development plans.

The European Commission has approved a EUR 212 million (USD 242 million) French State aid scheme to support agricultural and aquaculture companies facing increased fuel prices due to the Middle East crisis. The scheme was approved under the Middle East Crisis Temporary State Aid Framework (METSAF) adopted by the Commission on 29 April 2026
The EU has paid EUR 34 million (USD 39 million) to Armenia to help its private sector deal with the impact of Russia’s trade restrictions.

China has launched a comprehensive 18-point action plan to stabilise employment, expand job opportunities and strengthen workforce resilience, with a strong focus on graduate recruitment, skills development and preparing workers for an AI-driven economy.

China's commerce ministry, alongside other government departments, released an action plan on Monday to stabilize and optimize foreign investment utilization. The action plan details 15 measures to be taken across five areas, which include expanding market access, facilitating investment procedures, enhancing investment promotion, strengthening services and guarantees for foreign investment, and improving foreign capital management.

Announced the launch of the Strategic Response Fund (SRF) call for proposals, inviting Canadian organizations and industry partners to apply for transformative investments that will strengthen the nation's food supply chains and industrial capacity. Through the SRF, the government is making up to USD 350 million available to advance Canada's National Food Security Strategy and fund eligible projects with between $10 million and $50 million each. This initiative will support companies and organizations in food and beverage manufacturing, packaging, industrial systems, and critical input production across the country.

Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food, announced an investment of up to USD 892,122 for Amphoraxe Life Sciences Inc. through the AgriScience Program Projects Component. This funding will accelerate the development and testing of promising new antimicrobial peptide (AMP) formulations to address significant threats to poultry health.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: Announced the budget for the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development of NPR 49.92 billion (USD 327.5 million), down from NPR 57.48 billion (USD 376.9 million) in the previous year.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policy_description: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
policydecision_details: Announced that the land designated for the redevelopment of the Male’ Fish Market must be handed over to the government, even if the existing contract for the project has not been formally terminated.
policycategory: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets

policydecision_details: Implemented agricultural reforms to move from administrative management towards economic freedom and competition. One important area is land issues. According to the new procedure, openness and transparency are ensured in the allocation of land for agriculture, and an electronic auction system has been introduced. This allows farmers to exercise their right to use land on a legal and guaranteed basis. Most importantly, restrictions have been established on the groundless termination of land lease rights.

Enacted a national minimum wage for teachers of BRL 5,130 (USD 930) for a 40-hour workweek, raised the minimum wage for basic education following a 5.4 percent adjustment, and established a rule preventing future increases from falling below the inflation rate across the country.

Approved a constitutional amendment that would effectively ban the six-days week work arrangement, sending the proposal to the Senate for ratification. The proposal reduces Brazil's constitutionally set cap on weekly working hours from 44 to 40 and require two paid rest days per week. In Brazil, service workers are typically paid a fixed monthly salary rather than an hourly wage, as is more common in the United States. Because the amendment would prohibit employers from reducing those salaries to reflect the shorter schedule, employers would have to pay the same monthly wage for roughly 10 percent fewer hours of work.

Launched an urgent field immunization and animal identification campaign across the threatened pastoral communities of Jinba, Al-Markaz, and Al-Halawa in Masafer Yatta. On its initial deployment day, specialized veterinary teams systematically targeted , or inoculated, 4,300 sheep across 45 smallholder herds against the highly infectious foot-and-mouth disease (specifically the SAT-1 serotype variant). Concurrently, the mobile units are executing a comprehensive livestock tagging and registration protocol, inserting unique identification tags to formally document herd ownership, optimize animal disease traceability vectors, and prevent asset loss. This urgent veterinary response reduces livestock mortality overheads, preserves the localized production of essential meat and dairy products, and directly stabilizes rural livelihoods against escalating physical disruption and systemic resource displacement.

Executed an integrated pest management and containment campaign targeting the red palm weevil (Rhynchophorus ferrugineus). To arrest the spread of this highly destructive wood-boring insect, phytosanitary teams have systematically identified, excavated, and removed approximately 60 heavily infested palm trees from municipal gardens, highway medians, and public infrastructure spaces. The extracted plant biomass was safely routed to containment landfills for controlled bio-secure incineration and deep burial. To safeguard the remaining urban canopy, field crews are pairing targeted chemical canopy sprayings with the deployment of specialized pheromone traps to disrupt the weevil's mating cycle and continuously track population vectors across the metropolitan territory.

policy_description: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
policydecision_details: The Bangladesh Trade and Tariff Commission (BTTC) has formed a nine-member panel to investigate complaints of distortionary trade practices, including the dumping of foreign goods into Bangladesh’s market at artificially low prices.
policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures

policydecision_details: Signed a decree introducing a new mechanism of state support for the export of non-oil and non-gas products. The initiative provides reimbursement of customs clearance expenses for micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) exporting their goods abroad. The support will be administered by the Ministry of Economy on a quarterly basis following applications submitted by exporters.The measure represents another step in Azerbaijan's broader strategy to diversify its economy and reduce its reliance on hydrocarbons
The fuel excise was due to expire 30 June but has been extended by another month. The current 32 cents a litre discount will be reduced to 16 cents a litre.

Introduced its first transfer pricing safe harbour. Any taxpayer with annual turnover of up to NPR 1 arba (USD 7.5 million) who meets any one of the following three conditions:i) IT Service Exports: Maintain a minimum operating profit margin of 15 percent on IT service operating costs. ii) Intercompany Foreign Currency Loans: Set the interest rate at the specified reference rate plus 200 to 400 basis points; iii) Low-Value Intragroup Services: Apply a maximum markup of 5 percent on total cost. Once elected, the safe harbour is binding for five consecutive income years and cannot be revoked unless there is a material change in the nature of the transaction.
Announced that the benefits from the high fuel prices will be passed on to the public.
Approved a proposal to publish a long-awaited animal welfare draft bill in the Government Gazette. The bill, when passed, will replace the outdated Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Ordinance of 1907.

Kazakhstan’s Prime Minister has instructed authorities to take all necessary measures to prevent fuel shortages and curb schemes of illegal cross-border movement of petroleum products, the press service of the Kazakh government said.

Nearly a year after signing their Free Trade Agreement (FTA), India will lower the customs duty on ICE cars from as high as 110 per cent to as low as 10 per cent, based on engine capacity and fuel type. It will implement these reductions in phases, starting at 30 per cent in the first year and reaching 10 per cent across all engine capacities and fuel types in the fifth year. India has set a quota of 378,000 ICE cars for the first 15 years, with the annual limit ranging from 15,000 to 37,000 units. For cars exceeding this quota, it will reduce the customs duty from as high as 110 per cent to as low as 45 per cent over a period of ten years.
China's Ministry of Commerce announced on Friday that it will impose an additional 55 percent tariff on beef imported from Australia on top of existing tariff rates.

The Bulgarian Food Safety Agency (BFSA) has announced changes to the enhanced monitoring regime for incoming shipments of milk and dairy raw materials from European Union member states and third countries.

Announced that genuine squatters will be distributed land ownership certificates by Dashain this year. With the current government’s 100-day action plan, the processes of land measurement, data collection, identification of genuine squatters, land management and distribution of ownership certificates have been accelerated.

Approved changes to the procedure for reinbursing excess VAT. The document amends the provisions of the 2022 Cabinet of Ministers resolution governing the procedures for verifying the validity of VAT overpayments, as well as their reimbursement and refund. Under the updated rules, taxpayers will be able to use the confirmed amount of VAT overpayment not only for a refund to a bank account but also to offset import VAT liabilities and to settle arrears on other taxes.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Approved a draft Lemon Law aimed at strengthening consumer protection by making sellers more accountable for defective goods, allowing buyers to seek repairs, replacements or compensation more easily when products fail within a specified period. The new legislation shifts the burden of proof from consumers to sellers. Under the proposed law, if a product becomes defective within the legal warranty period, it will be presumed that the defect existed at the time of delivery unless the seller can prove otherwise.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policy_description: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination
policydecision_details: Launched an open-access, Caribbean Blue Economy (BE) Knowledge Hub, in collaborationn with FAO and the Development Bank of Latin America and the Caribbean, that brings together decades of the region’s expertise and insight on fisheries, aquaculture, and marine spatial planning. The knowledge hub is a permanent, multilingual home for Blue Economy data, best practices, policy tools, and technical insight from across the participating countries–Barbados, Belize, Guyana, Jamaica, Panama, and Saint Lucia—built on CRFM’s expertise and the knowledge generated through the BE-CLME+ Project.
policycategory: Unspecified policy for knowledge generation and dissemination

policydecision_details: Issued Resolution No. 197/2026 repealing Resolution No. 283/2015 and reistating the original working of the Patent Examination Guidelines concerning living matter and natural substances. The key development is the removal of the additional restrictions introduced in 2015, which for more than a decade contributed to a particularly restrictive framework for the protection of certain biotechnology inventions. The resolution also includes safeguards for good-faith third parties that, at the time the regulation entered into force, were already commercializing products covered by pending patent applications that may ultimately be granted as a consequence of this regulatory change.

Poland's lower house of parliament on Friday approved government legislation introducing a windfall tax on fuel companies, including state-controlled energy giant Orlen, in a move aimed at capturing what the government describes as extraordinary profits generated during periods of market disruption.

Released guidelines covering banks’ and electric money issuers’ (EMIs) digital marketplace activities, paving the way for them to offer products on a single platform to make the financial sector more inclusive and customer-centric.

Introduced a new set of regulations aimed at enhancing the monitoring and oversight of outward remittances associated with import transactions. he new measures are designed to improve transparency in import-related foreign exchange payments and enhance coordination between commercial banks and the Sri Lanka Customs Department.

Japan's parliament has passed a bill strengthening protection rights for new plant varieties, based on its determination that domestically developed agricultural varieties are being leaked overseas to countries including China and South Korea.

To ease the impact of Russian import restrictions on Armenian goods, the government has introduced a new support program for greenhouse farmers. The new relief program was adopted at a Cabinet meeting on June 18.
Notified that the Competition and Consumer Commission made the guidelines to interpret and give effect to the provision of Part 3.

The United States and Iran have reached a peace agreement to implement an immediate and permanent cessation of military operations. As part of this deal, the United States will remove its naval blockade of Iranian ports and reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping to facilitate the flow of energy and essential commodities like fertilizer.
contextoradditionalinfo: The blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, a vital route for global energy supplies, caused significant economic disruption, including inflated energy prices and supply chain congestion for essential agricultural inputs like fertilizer, threatening global food production.

policydecision_details: Approved regulations governing Labor Assistance Funds (FALs), a new mechanism designed to help private-sector employers manage severance payment obligations. Effective November 1, 2026, employers may contribute to authorized investment vehicles that fund severance payments for registered employees. Contributions will be integrated into social security reporting and may be tax-deductible. Additional implementing guidance is expected within 45 business days.

Launched an infrastructure project to supply the El Alem agricultural complex in the Sbeitla delegation with treated wastewater routed from the local municipal treatment plant. Backed by a capital investment of 870,000 dinars via the Regional Commission for Agricultural Development, the hydraulic engineering system integrates dedicated solar energy arrays to pump and distribute unconventional water resources across a 30-hectare fodder cultivation zone and 50 hectares of regional olive groves. This intervention delivers a climate-adaptive framework for the Kairouan governorate, which has faced severe groundwater depletion and protracted multi-year drought cycles, while simultaneously utilizing tertiary water treatment to sustain regional agrifood supply chains. Additionally, institutional monitoring confirmed that regional harvest operations have scaled to 40% completion at the complex and 79% across the broader governorate, accumulating roughly 550,000 quintals of grain at localized collection centers.

policy_description: Seed technology and quality assurance systems
policydecision_details: Entered into a strategic partnership agreement to enhance national seed sovereignty and accelerate the production of locally adapted pre-basic seeds. Formalized at the Marchouch experimental station, the collaborative framework directly aligns with the guidelines of the "Generation Green 2020-2030" strategy, which targets raising the utilization rate of certified seeds to 40% and increasing the market share of nationally developed plant varieties to 50% by 2030. Operating under joint strategic and technical governance committees, the integrated approach structures coordinated seed-requirement planning, rigorous quality monitoring across critical crop segments—including cereals, pulses, forage crops, and oilseeds—and unified commercialization pathways. This programmatic alignment aims to bolster agricultural competitiveness and provide farmers with resilient, climate-adapted plant genetics optimized for local soil and weather conditions.
policycategory: Seed technology and quality assurance systems

policydecision_details: Implemented an urgent intervention to support livestock breeders. Two truckloads of animal feed (45 large bales of hay, each weighing 450 kg) were distributed to the livestock breeders most affected in the Tubas Governorate and the northern Jordan Valley. This initiative is part of the Ministry's efforts to mitigate the impact of the difficult conditions faced by farmers and livestock breeders. The feed was delivered this morning to address some of the growing need for fodder in the region, particularly in light of the repeated attacks by settlers against farmers and livestock breeders in the northern Jordan Valley. These attacks have resulted in damage that has impacted their access to grazing lands and their ability to meet the needs of their livestock.
The Government of Mali and Japan, through the ILO, launch a project to combat child labour in Ségou.

The World Bank’s Board of Executive Directors today approved USD 1.5 billion in financing to support India’s structural reforms to boost private sector-led job creation and economic growth under the Boosting Job Creation in the Private Sector Development Policy Financing (DPF) Operation.
The Hungarian government is ending the era of protected fuel prices, as market prices have fallen below the state-imposed price caps.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: The government has launched a comprehensive set of programmes and long-term strategies to mitigate the impacts of climate change, with particular emphasis on water resource management, disaster resilience, renewable energy expansion and environmental protection. As part of climate mitigation efforts, he said, the government has launched a nationwide campaign to plant 25 crore trees over the next five years. Annual tree fairs are being organised at national, divisional, district and upazila levels, while a three-month tree plantation drive will also be implemented.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: The Government approved the Employment Assurance Program for Persons with Disabilities and Persons Over 63, the development of which is conditioned by the need to increase the employment opportunities of persons with disabilities of the 1st or 2nd group or profound or severe functional limitations and persons over 63, to increase their competitiveness in the labor market and to ensure stable employment.

Announced plnas for a new international financial centre and outlined six priority areas for attracting foreign investment. This initiative aims to strengthen legal protections for investors, expand capital markets and accelerate industrial development.
Announced a set of policy on the inspection and management of Or Tor Kor Market.

Approved the submission of five trade agreements aimed at strenghtening export competitiveness, widening market access and supporting long-term economic growth.They include two new free trade agreements, two upgraded regional trade pacts and one World Trade Organisation-related protocol on fisheries subsidies. The two new FTAs are the Thailand-European Free Trade Association Free Trade Agreement and the Thailand-Bhutan Free Trade Agreement. The upgraded agreements cover the Asean-China Free Trade Area and the Second Protocol to Amend the Asean Trade in Goods Agreement. The fifth agreement is the Protocol Amending the Marrakesh Agreement Establishing the WTO to incorporate the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies.

policy_description: Price intervention on cash crop commodities
policydecision_details: Established that the new producer price for cocoa for the 2026 Light Crop Season will remain unchanged, despite declining in global cocoa prices protecting farmers income during the harvest. The producer price will remain at GHD1,241.76 per load of 30 kilogrammes for Grade I and II cocoa beans (approximately USD119.21) and GHD2,587.00 per bag of 64 kilogrammes gross (approximately USd248.35). Consequently, a tonne of cocoa, equivalent to 16 bags, will continue to attract GHD41,392.00 (approximately USD3,973.63).
policycategory: Price intervention on cash crop commodities

policydecision_details: Signed a new co-operation deal with the US to combat drug trafficking: the US would provide up to USD 20million to train and equip Bolivian forces as part of a joint fight against drug smuggling.
Rejected the free trade dela between the European Free Trade Association states and the MERCOSUR states.

Parents who are raising their children alone will not be required to work at night. Additionally, parental leave will count towards the pension contribution period. These provisions are included in a package of legislative amendments approved by the government, which also involves the ratification of Convention No. 156 of the International Labour Organisation regarding workers with family responsibilities.
Kazakhstan detailed a comprehensive optimization plan for 2026–2030 targeting state and quasi-state assets with a combined revenue of 3.4 trillion tenge (USD 6.9 billion).

Onitiated the first distribution phase of a 1.5 million vegetable seedling project under the "Together for Food Security" campaign. Cultivated at the state nursery in Abdeh, Akkar, the initial cohort of 500,000 diversified seedlings is being systematically allocated via the National Farmers Registry and localized municipal networks to smallholders situated in climate-compatible zones exceeding 500 meters above sea level. This emergency agronomic intervention is a core element of the state's broader Agricultural Response and Recovery Plan, which interfaces with a macro-level UNDP program dedicated to reviving the seed production value chain at the Lebanese Agricultural Research Institute (LARI). Backed by a 153.3 million euro German humanitarian and development aid package designed to insulate vulnerable farming families from current crises, the state-led infrastructure project aims to revitalize dormant arable land, expand domestic crop yields, and stabilize national food security architecture.
The European Commission has approved an EUR 85 million (USD 98 million) Irish State aid scheme to support agricultural companies facing increased fuel prices due to the Middle East crisis.

European Commission has approved a EUR 1 billion Slovak aid scheme raises cleantech competitiveness stakes. The scheme will provide support through grants and income tax relief. It will be open to small and medium-sized enterprises as well as large companies investing to add manufacturing capacity for clean technologies .Support can be granted until 31 December 2030 under the EU’s Clean Industrial Deal State Aid Framework .

Parliament has adopted new rules facilitating access to new plants that are climate and pest resistant, give higher yields and require fewer pesticides. The amended rules for new genomic techniques (NGTs) were provisionally agreed between Parliament and Council in December 2025. The new EU rules mark a shift towards regulating plants on the basis of what they finally look like genetically and not how they were made. NGT-altered plants are to be split into two categories with different legal obligations.

policy_description: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
policydecision_details: Council of the European Union and the European Parliament reached a political agreement on the "Omnibus VI" package proposed by the European Commission. The agreement seeks to streamline regulations on cosmetics, the Classification, Labelling and Packaging of substances and mixtures (CLP), and EU fertiliser products.
policycategory: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs

policydecision_details: China's central bank governor Pan Gongsheng on Wednesday announced six new financial policy measures at the 2026 Lujiazui Forum.
Canada has introduced legislation to strengthen its forced labour import ban, replacing the current Customs Tariff framework with a standalone law.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Cabinet Committee on Government Purchase (CCGP) today approved the import of three cargoes of Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) aimed at meeting growing domestic energy demand and ensuring supply stability.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Implemented a wide-ranging reform to modernize agriculture sector through mechanisation, seed regulation, research, farmer support programmes and value-added exports.

country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
policydecision_details: UK and India have announced their landmark trade deal will enter into force next month so working people and businesses can benefit. Businesseswill be able to trade under its terms from July 15th.

Detailed a NTD 6.25 billion (USD 198 million) programme to expand social welfare programmes for older people (from 65) living alone. The initiative would provide home visits, meal deliveries and functional assessments.
Signed a decree eliminating citizen participation and transparency controls in the selection process for Supreme Court judges, modifying historic federal regulations.

Received the approval of a World Bank innovative financing package to support the reform agenda and help restore its access to international capital markets. The financing combines two World Bank Group guarantees to help mobilize up to USD 2 billion in commercial loans: a first-loss Policy-Based Guarantee (PBG) from the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) and a second-loss guarantee from the Multilateral Investment Guarantee Agency (MIGA). Together, the guarantees will cover 95% of debt service payments under the commercial loan, enabling Argentina to lower borrowing costs and strengthen public debt management.
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved a USD 500 million equivalent policy-based loan to support Kazakhstan in strengthening fiscal sustainability and enhancing financial sector resilience.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Secured a EUR 690 million financing package from European Union to modernize and scale up the national power grid. Structured as one of the inaugural flagship operations under the Trans-Mediterranean Renewable Energy and Clean-Tech Cooperation Initiative (T-MED), the capital deployment combines a €600 million loan with up to EUR 90 million in direct European Union grants.
