The macro-scale infrastructure modernization framework is designed to integrate 22 gigawatts (GW) of new renewable energy generation capacity into the domestic grid architecture by 2030—effectively securing clean power access for approximately 10 million households while positioning the country as a competitive, cross-border Mediterranean energy transmission hub.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Launched an extensive multi-sectoral financing and stabilization initiative for the 2026 summer cropping season, mapping out an ambitious cultivation plan targeting over 31 million feddans across decentralized states like Sennar. Implemented to directly counter the severe infrastructural destruction and vegetation degradation left by conflict zones, the rehabilitation strategy introduces a mandatory technology-linked lending mechanism that bundles microfinance, capital allocations, and advanced extension programs with formal agricultural insurance through a dedicated Risk Mitigation Fund. To alleviate the heavy economic constraints bearing down on smallholders and organized cooperative associations, the coordinated banking framework leverages capital instruments and subsidized fuel proposals alongside targeted fertilizer and seed distributions, prioritizing high-efficiency organized farming structures to reinforce macro food security.

Implemented a large-scale campaign in several provinces to reduce the number of stray dog on streets. This campaign is part of a government plan to enhance public safety. It also responds to increasing complaints from citizens about the growing number of animals in residential areas.

Parliament approved new rules to strengthen the contractual position of farmers and help stabilise their incomes. MEPs endorsed new rules to ensure that the final prices of food products better reflect the actual costs and have a direct impact on farmers’ incomes. Member states will be required to establish and publish online benchmarks for use in contractual arrangements.
Bill C-37, the proposed First Nations Clean Water Act, was introduced in the House of Commons on June 16, 2026.
The government has introduced the National Poultry Development Policy-26 with the aim of making country’s poultry sector more modern, safe, environmentally sustainable and export-oriented.

Azerbaijan and Mongolia have agreed to significantly expand cooperation in international road transportation, including a substantial increase in permit quotas for freight carriers and plans to introduce an electronic permit exchange system.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: All seven provincial governments announced their allocation for agricultural budget. A common resolution seen in the budgets of all seven provinces is to modernize, mechanize, commercialize, and make the agricultural system, which is a traditional means of livelihood, technology-friendly, thereby laying the foundation for a self-reliant economy.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Moved to establish its first comprehensive legal framework governing digital identity and cybersecurity, as lawmakers advanced legislation aimed at securing online services, protecting personal data, and strengthening the country’s defenses against cyber threats.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: Maintained its price control list of 66 essential goods and services for another year to protect consumers from price volatility. While the list of items remains the same, supervisory measures will be tightened for certain products, including young coconuts, soybean meal, animal feed maize, onions, and garlic. Controls will be relaxed for items where market conditions have normalized, such as alcohol-based hand sanitizers, face masks, and ATK test kits.

Approved in principle two significant international measures: Thailand’s engagement with the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)‘s Global Anti-Base Erosion (GloBE) Rules — the legal framework underpinning the 15 percent Global Minimum Tax (GMT) agreed by over 135 jurisdictions. These developments carry significant implications for multinational enterprise (MNE) groups operating in or through Thailand, as well as for international investors monitoring Thailand’s regulatory trajectory.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Launched a central net-zero training hub, which aims to expand the workforce needed to meet Taiwan’s 2050 net-zero emissions target. The center is part of a broader national alliance spanning 37 universities and four regional hubs.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Approved amendments to selected provisions of the Waste Disposal Act to enhance resource circulation and curb illegal wate dumping. In addition to complementing the newly enacted Resource Circulation Promotion Act and establishing a stronger legal foundation for Taiwan's circular economy, the amendments comprehensively strengthen the management of emerging waste streams, industrial waste reuse mechanisms, and environmental crime prevention measures, demonstrating the government's determination to advance resource circulation, safeguard environmental justice, and protect land and environment.

Unveiled agreements to purchase agricultural products and fishery products from several Taiwan, Province of China counties governed by the Chinese Nationalist Party (KMT). The deals involve products such as atemoyas, pomeloes, tea and grouper from Taitung, Yunlin and Nantou counties.

Announced measures to become the first country in the Americas to export spring mangoes from officially designated fruit-flu-free zone. This effort is particularly crucial for exports to the United States, which enforces stringent phytosanitary regulation to permit fresh fruit imports.

Begun signing farmers to a 16-crop production program aimed at reducing the country's annual primary produce import bill, which currently ranges between USD 80 million and USD 100 million. The program focuses on beet, butternut squash, cabbage, cantaloupe, carrots, cassava, cucumber, lettuce, onion, hot pepper, sweet pepper, pumpkin, sweet potato, tomato watermelon and yam. Four crops (cucumber, cassava, sweet potato and yam) already require minimal imports due to existing domestic production.

Published the official regulations for CBS and IBS, the new taxes introduced under Brazil’s Dual VAT Tax Reform model. Following this approval, major electronic tax documents must include the information required by both taxes. This change requires updates to layouts, validation rules, and electronic invoicing systems. Affected documents include NF-e, NFC-e, NFS-e, CT-e, CT-e OS, BP-e, MDF-e, NFCom, NF3e, GTV-e, and DC-e, among others. In addition, Technical Note 2025.002-RTC v1.40 establishes that companies operating under the General Tax Regime must report IBS and CBS groups in NF-e and NFC-e documents. Failure to comply with this requirement may result in document rejections in the production environment.

Introduced a significant overhaul of its Used Production Lines Import Regime, expanding investment opportunities for manufacturers, energy companies, logistics operators, and industrial groups seeking to modernize operations while lowering capital costs (Decree No 438/2026). While the reform broadens access to the regime, it also introduces stricter compliance requirements and stronger enforcement mechanisms.

country: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland
policydecision_details: British Prime Minister Keir Starmer has announced a sweeping ban on social media use for those under 16, joining other countries around the world seeking to protect children online.
The National Agency for Food Safety (ANSA) announces the launch of a new approach to managing risks associated with African swine fever through a national assessment of small-scale pig farms.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: New Zealand's Natural Hazards Commission Toka Tū Ake (NHC) has arranged a record NZ$12.3 billion (USD 7 billion) in reinsurance protection for the coming year, strengthening the financial buffer available to homeowners if a major natural hazard disaster occurs.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Announced that more than 80,000 hectares of land will be allocated to investors starting next agricultural season to accelerate the production of strategic crops. This major land allocation will be progressively executed upon the completion of substantial, ongoing public infrastructure upgrades—including a 3-billion-dinar agricultural electrification initiative to install 425 kilometers of electrical grids and 233 transformers, alongside a secondary 2-billion-dinar network expansion. To manage the anticipated surge in Saharan crop yields, the province has built nine local grain storage hubs with a combined capacity of 450,000 quintals and is currently constructing a massive strategic silo capable of holding one million quintals. These structural expansions, paired with crop diversification efforts like the cereal and industrial sugar beet operations at the "Tafadis" farm run by the Madar Group, aim to transform the region into a high-performance agricultural hub that strengthens national food security.

Received a shipment of 20,000 tissue-cultured date palm offshoots as part of a long-term contract with the British agritech specialist D.P.D. Limited. Delivered under the National Program for the Rehabilitation and Development of Date Palms and the Propagation of Tissue Culture Offshoots, the batch contains elite and popular regional varieties including Barhi, Zamli, Shishi, and Khalas. This specialized agricultural procurement utilizes micro-propagation biotechnology to supply disease-free, high-yielding trees intended to revitalize historic orchards, improve fruit quality, and bolster crop diversity. By integrating advanced international science into domestic cultivation plans, the institution aims to scale production efficiency, expand farming acreage, and enhance regional food supply resilience.

Approved USD 105 million projects in prevention, detection and sterile fly technology to expand screwwom defense efforts. Among the projects are initiatives to expand the use of drones for surveillance, improve wound-detection capabilities in livestock, develop more efficient sterile fly production techniques, enhance monitoring systems, and evaluate low-level insecticide applications as preventative tools. The breadth of the portfolio suggests USDA is pursuing both immediate operational improvements and longer-term technological advances that could strengthen the nation's biosecurity posture against future incursions

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Received the approval for an additional financing of €400 million (USD468.4 million)from World Bank to scale up Türkiye’s distributed renewable energy market, expanding support for distributed wind power and commercial-scale battery storage.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Irish Minister for Agriculture Martin Heydon has announced a €2 million (US$2.3 million) fuel support scheme for specialist fruit and vegetable growers. The scheme is expected to open next week and forms part of the €100 million (US$113.6 million) allocated by the Irish government for fuel income supports for farmers, fishers, and agricultural contractors in response to the Middle East crisis.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: Greece will invest more than EUR 20 billion (USD 23 billion) in its agricultural sector over the next six years, Rural Development and Food Minister announced, framing the package as both a domestic modernization drive and a strategic position ahead of negotiations over the European Union's next Common Agricultural Policy.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: Croatian veterinary authorities have expanded restriction zones after confirming a new outbreak of peste des petits ruminants (PPR), also known as sheep and goat plague, in the settlement of Donji Dragičevci near Čazma in Bjelovar-Bilogora County.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The Croatian government has allocated funding for the energy renovation of 269 multi-apartment buildings as part of efforts to mitigate the impact of the energy crisis. Following the government’s decision, the latest public call will result in the implementation of energy efficiency measures in a total of 411 buildings.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Cambodia has launched an Agri-Input Financing Programme to improve farmers’ access to quality agricultural inputs and strengthen linkages between farmers, suppliers, and the wider agricultural value chain. The initiative aims to support increased agricultural productivity, improved household incomes, stronger food security, and more sustainable rural development across Cambodia.

Updated poultry import rules following HPAI developments. Imports of ornamental birds, poultry and poultry products from the Netherlands are now suspended. Previous suspensions on Canada, Hungary, Japan and the USA have been lifted. Heat-treated poultry products that comply with WOAH guidelines remain exempt.

Granted a six-month grace period to bring existing market stock into compliance with the new labeling regulations ans substandards for food packing, which mandates that all food items must be packaged exclusively using food-grade materials. Violators will face, after the grace period, criminal charges and fines op to MVR 1 million (USD 64 700).
Lifted temporary restrictions on steel exports.

Issued an official regulatory alert prohibiting the use of untreated sewage water for the irrigation of agricultural land. The regional enforcement directive underscores that the deployment of non-potable wastewater in primary crop production explicitly violates the statutory provisions and executive regulations of the national Agriculture System Law. Designed to insulate local aquifers from environmental contamination, uphold strict public food safety standards, and protect consumers from soil-borne pathogenic risks, this public health intervention reinforces the state's legal framework governing sustainable resource management.

In collaboration with FAO, provided productive assets and agricultural inputs to rural women and farmers in Karbala Governorate. Implemented through two climate-smart and livelihood-focused projects funded by Norway and the Green Climate Fund, the initiative distributed specialized dairy processing equipment to 300 rural women to improve the milk value chain and minimize product losses. Additionally, agricultural fertilizers and technical support were provided to 140 beneficiaries to optimize vegetable production and promote sustainable resource management. This cross-border and localized initiative aims to strengthen climate resilience, advance women's economic empowerment, and secure regional food systems.

policy_description: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
policydecision_details: Indonesia's Minister of Finance has issued new regulations on antidumping customs duty (BMAD) for duplex paperboard products from the Republic of Korea, Malaysia, and Taiwan. This policy is outlined in Minister of Finance Regulation (PMK) Number 40 of 2026.
policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures

policydecision_details: Poland decided to extend a VAT cut and price caps on gasoline and diesel ​till the ​end ⁠of June, but did not extend reductions in ​excise duty.

policy_description: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets
policydecision_details: Launched a series of strategic marketing initiatives to manage the commencement of the annual fresh date harvest across the Al-Ahsa Oasis. Accelerated by high summer temperatures that drive early crop ripening, the region’s agricultural network is actively sorting and distributing over 20 distinct palm varieties, drawing from an expansive ecological matrix of more than two million palm trees that yield over 120,000 tons of dates annually. To optimize the supply chain and bolster economic returns for local farmers, public authorities have deployed specialized field teams to directly oversee commercial auction processes while establishing seasonal date festivals and integrated farmers' markets to connect local producers with domestic and regional trade networks.
policycategory: Promotion of farmer markets or community markets

policydecision_details: Launched the seasonal cereal harvest campaign at the "Global Agrodiv" farm, a flagship agricultural development project managed by the Madar Group in the Ouargla province. To accommodate the expanding yield of these strategic Saharan crops, the state has deployed significant heavy machinery and logistics while completing 400 kilometers of new farm tracks and over 900 kilometers of agricultural electrification networks. Additionally, the initiative expanded local storage capacity with the launch of two new grain collection hubs totaling 100,000 quintals and an intermediate silo complex to improve crop preservation, enhance national food security, and diversify regional industrial crops like sugar beets.

Announced that the government has expanded the Export Finance Scheme (EFS) to PKR 88 billion (USD 309 million), meaning the State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) will allocate more subsidised capital to support local businesses in the next fiscal year.

Approved early procurement of fertiliser raw materials to enable the country to secure fertiliser supplies months before fresh geopolitical tensions disrupted global shipping routes and pushed up prices of key agricultural inputs. Granular Ammonium Sulphate was secured at USD 228 per metric tonne against a current market price of USD 343 per tonne, while Diammonium Phosphate was purchased at USD 775 per tonne compared to the prevailing USD 950 market rate. Similarly, Muriate of Potash was acquired at USD 400 per tonne, lower than the current market price of $430 per tonne. PFI NPK disclosed that it secured nine vessels carrying a combined 407,304 metric tonnes of fertiliser raw materials during the first quarter of 2026.

Distributed free fertilisers to 20 160 South-west farmers (approximately 80 640 bags). The intervention, implemented under the federal government’s Renewed Hope Farm Input Support Programme (FISP), was officially flagged off in Ado-Ekiti as part of measures to support farmers during the 2026 wet farming season. All fertilisers distributed under the programme were locally produced, traceable and clearly branded “Not For Sale” to curb diversion and ensure accountability.

Eased immigration rules, under Decree No. 531, reducing the annual residency requirements for temporary residents from nine months to 90 days. The change aims to attract entrepreneurs, investors, and remote workers. Overseas income and Bitcoin capital gains are taxed at 0%, with no wealth, inheritance, or gift taxes. On-chain data indicates rising interest in the region. Investors should monitor the Fear & Greed Index for shifts in market sentiment. Tax obligations in home countries remain a key consideration.

Approved the increased government spending for the next fiscal year by 30 percent, helped by revenue from the mining sector and a diversification of its exports, for a total budget of CFA 7.02 trillions (USD 2.63 billion) for the 12 months starting from July.

Entered into a 10-year strategic cooperation agreement to operate the Al Alamiya Oil Industry Factory in Hama. Designed to serve as a primary industrial hub for the country's edible oil, food, feed, poultry, and livestock sectors, the facility is slated to process approximately 300,000 tonnes of soybeans and 100,000 tonnes of sunflower seeds annually, yielding an estimated production value of USD 500 million. Under this operational framework, the international agribusiness firm will leverage its global supply chain and logistics expertise to optimize factory performance while implementing structured workforce development programs. Notably, the agreement mandates that local citizens represent at least 75% of both technical and managerial personnel, ensuring a direct transfer of operational know-how to build independent domestic capacity over time.

Lifted quarantine measures linked to an infectious disease that prompted the culling of approximately 90,000 cattle across nine regions earlier this year. The regional agriculture ministry confirmed that meat and livestock that have passed veterinary inspection can now be freely sold and transported within the region, while external movement will resume after the area's health status is restored. The culls were officially attributed to rabies and a mutated form of pasteurellosis.
Presented the 2027 General Budget, focused on economic diversification and job creation.

The Japanese government and private sector are preparing to launch a dedicated organization to manage plant variety rights, with operations expected to begin in August. The initiative aims to address the unauthorized overseas use of Japanese fruit and vegetable varieties and to strengthen the collection of royalties from licensed production.

The European Union (EU) has lifted its import restrictions on fresh and processed poultry meat from Bosnia and Herzegovina related to highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI). The restrictions were introduced in February 2026. Bosnia and Herzegovina has now demonstrated that these products no longer represent a threat to animal health in the EU.

The Armenian government has approved a third package of subsidies aimed at supporting domestic exporters, with a focus on shipments to markets including the European Union. On June 4, the government approved two earlier subsidy packages, including compensation for logistics costs and customs payments. Under the first package, subsidies are provided to offset logistics expenses for exports of greenhouse-grown fresh fruits and vegetables, as well as flowers. Under the second package, the government agreed to compensate customs duties for entrepreneurs exporting fruits, vegetables, and flowers to the EU, the United Kingdom, and Canada.

Hong Kong is introducing a new package of tax and maritime incentives aimed at strengthening its position as a regional trading hub and supporting the transition to greener shipping, amid ongoing global supply chain pressures.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Developed a comprehensive regulatory framework for the country's biomethane sector, including a new Official Mexican Standard (NOM) covering quality specifications, grid injection protocols and supply chain traceability.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Planned to increase tax revenues while keeping the budget deficit within WAEMU limits. Authorities are targeting an average tax-to-GDP ratio of 14.6 percent over the period. The ratio is expected to rise from 13.9 percent in 2027 to 14.7 percent in 2028 and 15.1 percent in 2029.

Announced to increase or implement new taxes to generate some USD 800 million in additional revenue a year to offset a surge in oil prices. The proposals include a 30 percent income tax hike for three years on companies in the Caribbean country that earn more than USD 17 million a year. Other proposals include a USD 10 increase on airline tickets and additional taxes on casinos, gambling and electronic cigarettes.

Announced a package of economic reforms aimed at attracting investment, expanding participation by Cubans living abroad in the economy and decentralizing parts of the country's administration. The government is also evaluating measures related to foreign trade, exports, supply chains and logistics.

Approved the commercialization of the genetically modified corn event COR-ØØ121-4, from Corteva Seeds Argentina, designed to control lepidopteran pests. The approval was formalized under Resolution No. 80/2026, following biosafety, food and feed safety, as well as trade impact assessments conducted by the country’s regulatory authorities.

Conclusion No. 18-KL/TW, adopted at the second meeting of the 14th Party Central Committee, established a 10–12% growth target in export turnover for the agriculture, forestry, and fisheries sectors during the 2026–2030 period.

The Council of the EU has approved the allocation of EUR 120.55 million (USD 137 million) from the European Union Solidarity Fund (EUSF) to Spain to help address the severe environmental, social and economic damage caused by the third wave of forest fires that swept across Spain in 2025. This wave of fires was the most destructive on record, with a total of 243 forest fires across 16 autonomous communities.
Slovenia lifted an arms embargo on Israel and entry bans on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and two of his ministers.

Romania's Parliament has approved the extension of the price-capping mechanism for 17 categories of basic food products until December 31, 2026, shifting responsibility for one of the country's key anti-inflation measures from the executive to the legislature.

On June 11, 2026, the Parliament of the Republic of Moldova passed, in its final reading, a law on geographical indications, guaranteed traditional specialties, and voluntary quality labels. The new regulation is intended to bring national legislation into line with European Union rules and strengthen the protection of Moldovan products with high added value.

The Cabinet adopted the Decree on quick-frozen foodstuffs intended for human consumption, with the aim of ensuring the implementation of the Law on Food Safety and achieving full alignment of national legislation with the European Union acquis in this area.

Kazakhstan is set to introduce mandatory veterinary passports for apiaries under newly approved legislation designed to modernise the country’s beekeeping sector and strengthen support for sustainable agricultural development. The law establishes a comprehensive regulatory framework for beekeeping, focusing on the protection, management and reproduction of bee populations while improving productivity and industry standards across the country.

Together with UNDP, launched a major food security project to produce and distribute 1.5 million vegetable seedlings to vulnerable domestic farming networks. Funded by the German government through the German Development Bank (KfW) as part of a larger 153.3 million euro humanitarian and development aid package, the initiative utilizes state-run nurseries—such as the Al-Abdeh facility in Akkar—to distribute high-quality agricultural inputs to growers registered in the National Farmers' Registry. The climate-matched distribution strategy scales up local agrifood production capacities, rehabilitates vital wheat seed value chains, and expands cultivated land area across diverse governorates to insulate rural communities from compounding supply shocks.

Lifted import restrictions and resume receiving Lebanese agricultural shipments, classifying the trade reopening as a pivotal development for national economic recovery and rural socioeconomic stability. By restoring direct access to this high-value commercial network, the regulatory milestone is projected to rapidly revitalize domestic packaging, transport, and cultivation supply lines while incentivizing the ministry to enforce stringent food safety oversight, product traceability, and international quality standards.

Approved an emergency support project for Lebanon to mitigate severe agricultural infrastructure damage and production losses. Designed to stabilize local food networks and maintain the continuity of rural livelihoods, the emergency recovery framework deploys specialized technical and financial aid portfolios to restore disrupted livestock breeding, secure the vulnerable beekeeping sector, and rehabilitate compromised agrifood supply lines.

Officially established the nationwide cereal reception pricing structure for the current harvest and storage campaign, embedding tiered financial incentives to accelerate crop collection. Under this framework, durum wheat is priced at JOD 140 (USD 198) per quintal (inclusive of a JOD 40 (USD 56) expedited delivery bonus), soft wheat is set at JOD 110 (approximately USD 155) per quintal (inclusive of a JOD 30 (USD 42) expedited delivery bonus), and barley and triticale are valued at JOD 90 (USD 127) per quintal (inclusive of a JOD 25 (USD 35) expedited delivery bonus). To secure these maximum payout rates, agricultural producers must comply with staggered seasonal delivery deadlines, with barley and triticale allocations requiring mid-summer submission, while durum and soft wheat eligibility extends into late summer.

Launched a major restocking initiative to release one million common carp fingerlings into natural water bodies. Executed in strategic partnership with the private sector specifically the Iraqi Fish Producers Association—the conservation and aquaculture project aims to significantly enhance inland fisheries and support regional food security. The first phase of the rollout commenced with the release of an initial 100,000 fingerlings in the wetlands of the Maysan Governorate. These juvenile fish were produced through specialized artificial breeding techniques at the Golden Fish Hatchery located in the Al-Madain District, southeast of Baghdad. The ministry intends to proceed with successive phased releases across strategic waterways until the total target of one million carp is achieved, replenishing aquatic ecosystems and sustaining livelihoods for local fishing communities.

A number of staple food categories will continue to be sold in Romania at capped prices, according to a law passed by Parliament. This is an extension of a social protection measure taken against the background of high inflation and a decrease in people’s purchasing power.

Prime Minister, Mark Carney, launched Canada's first-ever National Food Security Strategy. Backed by more than USD 3 billion in investments over ten years, this strategy will break open the market for independent retailers, boost domestic food production, and build a stronger, more independent, and more affordable food system for all Canadians.
The cabinet has approved the Thailand-Bhutan free trade agreement (FTA), which is expected to take effect early next year.

The National Assembly held the re-deliberation on the Livestock Bill of Bhutan 2025 today. The Member-in-Charge of the Bill, the Minister for Agriculture and Livestock, moved the motion for re-deliberation. The Bill was adopted by the National Assembly on 3 December 2025 and transmitted to the National Council. The National Council adopted the Bill with amendments on 8 June 2026 and transmitted it back to the National Assembly for re-deliberation.

On the afternoon of June 11, at Tien Sa Port in Da Nang City, the Viet Nam Disaster and Dyke Management Authority coordinated with the Quang Tri Provincial People's Committee to receive an international aid shipment from the Government of the Republic of Belarus intended to support residents affected by disasters in the province.

Finance Minister announced a series of customs and trade facilitation measures, including extending custom bond facilities to all export-oriented sectors beyond ready-made garments and withdrawing the 10 percent supplementary duty on imports of synthetic woven fabrics.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: Finance and Planning Ministe made the announcement while unveiling the national budget of 2026-27 in parliament.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: Russia will restrict imports of most food, seeds, flowers, wood and fertilizer from Armenia starting on June the 12th. The federal agricultural safety agency said the sweeping ban was issued in response to the “systematic detection” of pests in products imported from Armenia since May. It claimed that, in June alone, three separate cases of khapra beetle infestations were discovered in dried food shipments.

The Council of Ministers has approved the National Action Plan for Persons with Disabilities 2026–2030. The document defines the policy framework for rights protection, social inclusion and independent living for persons with disabilities over the next five years.
Unveiled a comprehensive package of tax exemptions and incentives aimed at promoting the adoption of electric vehicles and natural-gas powered transports.

Presented the FY 2026/2027 budget, totalling TZS 62.33 trillion (USD 231 billion), 10.3 percent higher than the previous year. New businesses, farmers, manufacturers, airlines and investors are among the main beneficiaries of the budget.

Announced the extension of a cap on commercial mark-up on staple foods by the end of the year. This is an extension of a social protection measure taken against the background of high inflation and a decrease in people’s purchasing power. Under this recent decision, traders will continue to respect the limits imposed on commercial mark-ups added to a list of food products considered essential. These include white bread, milk, eggs, fresh chicken and pork, as well as a number of fruits and vegetables sold in bulk. The list includes products such as tomatoes, onions, cucumbers and beans, but also fruits such as apples, pears, plums and grapes.

Announced that had secured USD 250 million IMF credit facility. The loan agreement involves a 38-month program to help Kigali adapt to tighter global financing conditions while sustaining growth. Rwanda's economy grew 9.4% last year but inflation hit 13% in April, far exceeding the National Bank of Rwanda's 2-8% target rang

Doubled its fertilizer subsidy budget to RwF 64 billion (approximately USD 45.6 million), as it moves to protect farmers from rising global prices and potential supply disruptions linked to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

Launched a partnership aimed at expanding farmer access to agricultural machinery thorugh structured leasing arrangements. The agreement provides a framework for both organisations to promote affordable access to tractors, harvesters, irrigation systems, processing equipment and other agricultural assets for farmers, cooperatives and agribusinesses
Sustained investements and increased exploration activities to target crude oil production output of 2.5 million barrels per day.

Approved the 2026/2027 budget. The government has proposed KSh 16.7 billion (approximately USD 128.6 million) to support manufacturing initiatives aimed at expanding industrial capacity and strengthening value chains. Key allocations include KSh 2.6 billion (approximately USD 20.0 million) for County Integrated Agro-Industrial Parks, KSh 5.4 billion (approximately USD 41.6 million) for the Supporting Access to Finance and Enterprise Recovery (SAFER) Project, and KSh 2.4 billion (approximately USD 18.5 million) for Kenya Jobs and Economic Transformation initiatives. Other investments include funding for textile hubs in Athi River and Naivasha, Export Processing Zones, and special economic zones aimed at deepening industrial clustering and boosting export competitiveness.

Announced a nationwide reduction in the price of domestic beer for the duration of the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The executive directive, which also applies to domestic wine, aims to boost morale as the global football tournament unfolds across the United States, Mexico, and Canada between June 11 and July 19, 2026.

Approved a decree classifying lithium as a strategic mineral, raising royalties on producers from 3.5 percent to 10 percent of gross revenue. Tantalum, niobium, tungsten, uranium, and rare earth elements were added to the higher-tax category simultaneously.

Announced a decree that could turn 3 982 old mining authorizations into formal administrative mining contracts, even though many have not fully adapted to the current mining law. The draft decree would set procedures and deadlines to convert ATEs into administrative mining contracts, a move the government frames as a way to give legal certainty and reduce red tape.
Under Decree 201/2026/ND-CP, the export tax rate on fluorite containing more than 97% calcium fluoride by weight (HS code 2529.22.00) will be reduced from 10% to 5%.

Signed a strategic funding agreement under the "Strengthening Livelihoods, Infrastructure, and Food Systems (LIFT)" program, financed by the Swedish organization We Effect. The infrastructure rehabilitation project in the town of Aqaba involves reconstructing 4 kilometers of vital agricultural access roads alongside modernizing local water utility networks by equipping licensed wells with solar energy systems and high-efficiency pipelines. Designed as a long-term development framework spanning from late 2025 through 2029, the structural intervention lowers regional transport costs, reduces fossil fuel dependencies for irrigation pumps, and expands land cultivation capabilities to reinforce smallholder food security.

Issued an official regulatory directive to halt all poultry imports until further notice. This protectionist policy measure is strategically designed to insulate the domestic livestock market from international trade competition, safeguard the broader poultry sector from commercial volatility, and provide critical market support to local breeders and small-scale livestock producers.

In collaboration with FAO, launched the AGRI-FIT innovation project. This pioneering national initiative is designed to promote inclusive and accessible agricultural systems by deploying innovative, adapted soilless farming techniques and modified greenhouse infrastructure specifically engineered for persons with motor disabilities. Aligned with Jordan's Economic Modernisation Vision and international Sustainable Development Goals, the project aims to dismantle physical and structural barriers to entry within the agricultural economy, providing independent, sustainable income streams and advancing targeted economic empowerment and social inclusion. By utilizing customized vertical or soilless nurseries that eliminate conventional labor limitations, the multi-institutional partnership establishes a scalable model for inclusive rural development and equitable workforce integration across Jordan's agrifood sector.

Launched a strategic investment roadmap designed to accelerate development in Qatar's agriculture and agrifood sector. Developed over a year-long consultative period with public and private stakeholders, the framework provides actionable guidance for policymakers and investors to strengthen food security, optimize supply chain logistics, and build resilient food systems through both localized production and targeted emerging international market assets. The initiative introduces specialized evaluation tools to help investors identify high-value agricultural commodities across various geographies, positioning Qatar as a regional hub for agrifood innovation, economic diversification, and sustainable commercial returns.

Signed two new financing operations of €100 million with the European Investment Bank for on-lend the funds to Turkish small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and mid-caps for renewable energy and energy efficiency investments. The EIB financing will support projects that reduce emissions of greenhouse gases, strengthen supply chains and energy security, enhance climate resilience, and create new green jobs in Türkiye.

Within the framework of the implementation of a new concessional financing mechanism for farmers conducting annual crops in Azerbaijan, the portion of the annual interest rate on loans taken for crop purposes up to 19 percent will be financed from the state budget, and farmers will only repay the principal debt at the end of the credit term.
Announced stricter export controls on Artificial Intelligence (AI) chip sales to China, to further align with United States measures.

Launched a raft of family support measures as part of its new population strategy, in response to the national security crises posed by decining birth rates. These measures address the challenges arising from demographic change, strengthen support and investment in future generations, and elevate childbearing and childrearing responsibilities to the level of national development policy. Focusing on three stages of family life—childbirth, childrearing and education—the initiative establishes a more comprehensive support system and extends assistance for young people through age 22, making it easier to marry and start families. The measures consists of: i) a monthly NTD 5 000 (USD 160) subsidy per child from birth until age of 18; ii) increase in child care subsidies and childrearing allowances for children aged 0 to 2 and increased tuition subsidies and chiadrearing allowanced for children aged 2 to 6; iii) reduced student loan insterest rates from 1.775 percent to 0.775 percent and extended student loan grace periods from 1 to 2 years, iv) extended the lenght of marriage leave, maternity leave and parternity leave, by three additional months if both parents each take six months of unpaid leave with allowance; v) expand tax reilief for families with children and reserved 40 percent of social housing units for newlyweds and parents of young children.
Implemented a temporary ban on South African livestock imports following the worsening Foot and Mouth Disease outbreak.

Presented the Finance Bill 2026, including the following provisions: i) fairness for service in the protective services, ii) protection of private pensions; iii) national-purpose funds and accountable giving; iv) energy investment and marginal marine gas fields; v) tax administration, surcharges and credits; vi) gaming, liquor licences and clear rules; vii) strengthening fines for existing offences; viii) modernising filings and registrar general framework; ix) trade standards.

Announced the finalization of a new Strategic Plan for the Development of the Agricultural Sector (PEDSA 2036), which is expected to remain in effect for the next ten year, with one of its main priorities being the creation of favourable condiitons to attract private investment in the sector. The government aims to strengthen the state’s role in creating a more business-friendly environment through public policies, legislation, and institutional mechanisms that encourage private investment in agriculture and related sectors.
Removed 30 percent import tariff on Ecuadorian goods.
The Israeli Knesset has approved the confiscation of funds from Palestinian clearance revenues, in a step that could deepen the Palestinian Authority's financial crisis.

Conducted a specialized technical training program for 18 female livestock farmers in the town of Yabroud. Financed by the European Union under the broader "Strengthening the Skills and Practices of Livestock Breeders at All Stages of the Animal Value Chain in the West Bank – Palestine" project, the capacity-building initiative delivers focused instruction on advanced farm management protocols, hygiene practices, and safety mechanisms for processing and handling dairy products. By equipping rural women with standardized technical skills to reduce contamination risks and lower operational overheads, the structural intervention directly scales up regional production efficiency, elevates product quality for broader market opportunities, and reinforces smallholder household incomes.

Signed 13 strategic bilateral agreements between Saudi Arabia and Russia, totaling SAR 4.8 billion (USD 1.28 billion) in investment, to advance the food security, biotechnology localization, and supply-chain resilience targets of Saudi Vision 2030. Key structural provisions within the agreements mandate the domestic manufacturing and localization of veterinary vaccines to enhance regional biosecurity, the development of specialized broiler poultry strains to accelerate meat self-sufficiency, and the security of long-term grain and feed input supply chains. Additionally, the investment framework opens new international distribution channels for Saudi aquaculture and niche agricultural exports, establishing trade protocols for Russian firms to market and distribute Saudi shrimp, fish, camel milk derivatives, and specialty coffee products globally.

In coordination with FAO, GCF and UNDP, launched a specialized two-month climate change adaptation training programme in Jordan. Operating under the USD 33.25 million Building Resilience to Cope with Climate Change in Jordan (BRCCJ) project, the initiative targets 200 women from local communities across the Madaba, Karak, Tafileh, and Ma’an governorates within the climate-vulnerable Dead Sea Basin. The curriculum—comprising 30 specialized sessions peer-supervised by established local female leaders—is structurally designed to build a localized network of women leaders specialized in climate change adaptation, enhance community-level water-use efficiency in the agricultural sector, and safeguard rural livelihoods against severe regional water stress.

Accelerated an integrated suite of smart agronomical and afforestation initiatives designed to curb carbon emissions across the country's plant, livestock, and aquaculture sectors. Driven by advanced technological transitions—such as AI-based precision fertilization systems that minimize input waste and pollution—the ministry has deployed and monitored multiple sustainability projects targeted at carbon sequestration, organic fertilizer production, and blue carbon ecosystems. Key structural developments include targeted commercial fruit and forestry initiatives—such as the OQ Green project, the cultivation of carbon-capturing hackberry trees, and expansive lemon and jojoba plantations across Shalim and Al Wusta designed to combat desertification while drastically boosting domestic fruit yields. Additionally, specialized research at the Animal Production Research Centre has successfully optimized livestock feed efficiency using local moringa and palm resources, lowering production costs by over 58% to harmonize national agricultural expansion with long-term climate sustainability targets.
Lifted the temporary ban on imported poultry products from Argentina. This comes after Argentinian authorities resolved the outbreak of high pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) or bird flu.

The department of fertilizers has sought a 100% increase in fertilizer subsidy to ₹3.5 trillion(USD 36 billion) for FY27 from the finance ministry to offset mounting losses of manufacturers due to subsidized sales even their costs soar due to the West Asia war-induced disruptions.

Meat shops and meat sales outlets will be allowed to operate only from designated locations under the Livestock Bill of Bhutan 2025, which the National Council adopted today after members raised concerns over the scattered location of such businesses.
commodity1: Meat and other animal derived products

policydecision_details: Approved in the first reading a draft law that significantly tightens requirements for the protection of water bodies. The changes span several legislative acts and will directly affect tourism and fisheries. Key measures include a ban on dumping any waste, including construction debris, and on burning waste and leaves within water protection zones ; restrictions on cutting and destroying vegetation such as sea buckthorn, reeds, willow shrubs and other habitats for fish and wildlife; a ban on discharging untreated wastewater and a requirement for treatment facilities at guesthouses, resorts and other facilities in protected zones; tougher liability for environmental violations (waste dumping, water pollution, synthetic fishing nets, poaching, etc.), including penalties of up to 8 years in prison with confiscation of property; special restrictions for the shoreline of Lake Issyk-Kul.

Adopted a decree on the transfer of agricultural land for long-term lease improvement of mechanisms for their implementation.The decree plans to introduce a new system for providing agricultural land for lease, as well as put up another 100 thousand hectares for auction in 2026 on updated terms. At the same time, the emphasis will be on strengthening economic incentives for efficient use of land

Sigend a decree to boost development of intensive fruit orchards by introducing Islamic financing options and water-saving tax breaks. The decree outlines a comprehensive support framework to establish 172,000 hectares of industrial orchards and vineyards by the end of 2028 by helping farmers and entrepreneurs replace economically inefficient, low-yield plots.

policy_description: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
policydecision_details: Accelerated plans to localise fertiliser production in response to the ongoing global supply bottlenecks triggered by geopolitical tensions, while also pushing for a co-ordinated regional procurement system within Southern Africa, to insulate the region from volatile external shocks and escalating input costs.
policycategory: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs

policydecision_details: The government has launched a new round of dining discounts for elderly residents, collaborating with local non-governmental organizations and major restaurant chains to distribute food vouchers to approximately 70,000 seniors. The initiative targets single-living elderly, elderly couples, and socially isolated seniors across the city.

Settled a domestic-law bond maturity. This operation, carried out in a context of liquidity pressure, is intended to reassure bondholders and the state's ability to meets its obligation. Yhe role of this maturity within its domestic debt management strategy, as the country prepares to host an IMF mission tasked with assessing the fiscal trajectory and short-term financing needs.

Secured over KSh 20 billion (approximately USD 154 million) in investment from the European Union to significantly boost its national infrastructure. This substantial funding package is earmarked for major digital and connectivity projects, including the extension of the Blue Raman submarine cable. The initiative aims to lower connectivity costs, drive economic growth, and solidify Kenya's position as a regional digital hub.

Launched a USD 3.5 billion AgriConnect programme to boost food production. This major agricultural transformation programme is expected to improve food security for nearly three million people and create more than 2.6 million jobs by 2035. The compact focuses on key agricultural commodities, including cocoa, oil palm, rice, maize, and poultry, while also supporting sectors such as cashew, coconut, rubber, fisheries, and forestry.

Published a draft law that eliminates the Ministry of Agriculture as an independent entity and creates the Ministry of Agro-food, a super agency that consolidates agricultural production, the food industry, sugar and its derivatives, beverages and liquors, fishing and the forestry sector under a single authority.

The Government of Spain has activated the fourth edition of the 'Verano Joven' programme, providing young people aged 18 to 30 with discounts of up to 90% on bus and train tickets for travel during July, August, and September 2026. The measure aims to facilitate youth mobility, promote public transport, and support the tourism sector.
contextoradditionalinfo: The programme was first launched in 2023 to remove financial barriers to travel for young people, with previous editions showing high participation rates and positive impacts on youth autonomy and the tourism economy.

policydecision_details: Substantially expanded the urban green infrastructure, driving the nation’s total green area to 21.9 million square metres and increasing the average citizen's allocation of green space to 6.8 square metres. Designed to fulfill the environmental sustainability and urban planning metrics of the Qatar National Vision 2030, the multi-sector initiative encompasses the planned scaling of public parks to 156 installations alongside the widespread rollout of 1,864 water-efficient irrigation networks across 715 domestic farms. To catalyze a localized circular economy, municipal authorities simultaneously modernized national waste management operations, processing over 755,000 tonnes of municipal waste, recovering approximately 4 million tonnes of recycled construction aggregates, treating 10,470 tonnes of end-of-life tires, and generating 276,000 megawatt-hours of electricity via dedicated waste-to-energy facilities while yielding 34,213 tonnes of organic compost for agricultural replenishment.

Approved the Water Authority's latest long-term plan, which, for the first time, allows private entities to plan and develop large desalination plants. The overarching goal of the new plan is to enable the State of Israel to produce 2.3 billion cubic meters of desalinated water per year by 2050, and 2,75 billion cubic meters per year by 2075.
Announced a sweeping set of seasonal fire prevention measures, banning entry to forests and prohibiting any form of open flame activity across the city.
Kazakhstan's Ministry of Energy has allocated 402,300 tons of diesel fuel for the ongoing sowing campaign, the Kazakh government says.
The Indonesian government announced the deployment of approximately 280 million cocoa and coconut seedlings to cover 870,000 hectares of community plantation land.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: European Commission approved an important Italian state aid scheme worth EUR 23 billion (USD 26 billion) designed to support electricity generation from clean sources. Italy will support the production of electricity from renewable sources using various technologies, such as onshore wind, solar power or hydropower, to achieve the objectives of the Clean Industry Pact.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Denmark’s new government has announced a major transformation of the agricultural sector, with the pig industry at the center of the reform agenda. Key measures include a ban on tail docking, a full transition to group housing for sows, reduced antibiotic use, and a reduction in piglet exports. Industry representatives have already warned about potential risks to competitiveness and employment.

Following a confirmed finding of New World screwworm in a calf in Texas, the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) announced today that it will implement temporary import restrictions on livestock, including horses, from entering Canada from affected areas.
Belarus has changed the procedure for registering with the employment service. The relevant resolution was signed by Prime Minister Aliaksandr Turchyn, the government’s press service reported.

policy_description: Seed technology and quality assurance systems
policydecision_details: Approved the National Seed Policy, aiming at transform the seed sector, enhance agricultural productivity, and contribute significantly to national food and nutritional security. Its key objectives include increasing quality seed production, promoting hybrid and high-tech seed development, encouraging domestic and foreign investment, safeguarding plant breeders’ rights, supporting climate-smart agriculture, strengthening biotechnology research, and enhancing seed exports.
policycategory: Seed technology and quality assurance systems

policydecision_details: Decided to provide assistance equivalent to approximately USD 42.9 million to Nepal under the Extended Credity Facility (ECF) program.

Imposed large fines for illegal hunting and shooting of rare wild animals. Under the updated regulations, fines for killing animals listed in the Red Book are as follows: i) snow leopard – 2 million som (over 11.1 million tenge); argali (mountain sheep), maral (red deer), brown bear, Persian gazelle: 1.5 million som (more than 8.3 million tenge); red dog, Pallas’s cat), lynx: 50,000 som (approximately 278,500 tenge).

Planned to restrict the importation of USD4,5 billion worth of goods that can ordinarily be produced in Zimbabwe under a proposed new law aimed at boosting industrialisation, creating jobs and reducing pressure on the country’s foreign currency reserves.

Received clearence for USD 280 million to overhaul provincial roads and urban access roads across Argentina's Entre Rìos, with a nine-year grace period to give the province room to build before repayments bite, and a 21.5-year tail spreading the cost across more than two political cycles. For investors and lenders watching Argentina edge back toward international debt markets, deals like this matter as a signal. They show that subnational governments can still tap long-tenor, dollar-denominated capital on sensible terms even while the federal purse stays shut, and they keep a pipeline of work flowing to the contractors, materials suppliers and consulting engineers who’d otherwise be staring at empty order books.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Introduced financial penalties for operators that do not comply with the elemination of gas flaring across oil industry, as the country intensifies efforts to reduce methane emissions, while maintaining its position as one of Africa's leading oil producer. Beyond enforcement measures, Angola plans to implement a series of interventions aimed at accelerating emissions reductions across the sector. These include expanding leak detection and repair programmes, eliminating routine flaring, electrifying industrial facilities, deploying carbon capture and storage technologies, and investing in alternative energy pathways such as green hydrogen and biofuels.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Expanded the artificial rainfall enhancement network to 14 operational stations to strengthen national water security. Distributed across highly strategic topographic vectors including the Hajar Mountains, Musandam, and Dhofar, the infrastructure utilizes advanced chemical-free ionization technology to emit negative ions into the atmosphere, accelerating cloud condensation nuclei formation during suitable meteorological windows. This technological framework has successfully optimized seasonal precipitation yields, accelerated groundwater aquifer recharge rates, and mitigated dust pollution levels to bolster climate resilience across the country's arid zones. This report focuses on innovative water resource management, climate-adaptive technology deployment, and regional groundwater infrastructure; it is not related to the current Middle East conflict.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Approved new labeling regulations for synthetic stones used in jewelry, under Resolution No. 657. The rules require that jewelry containing artificial materials be clearly marked with the word "synthetic" on tags, prohibit the use of terms such as "diamond," "natural," or "eco-friendly" for lab-grown stones, and ban descriptions typically associated with natural diamonds. The measure aims to enhance consumer transparency, prevent misleading marketing, and support fair competition in the diamond industry.
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: Purchases USD 801 million after shekel reached a 33-year peak against the dollar, raising fears of tech firm layoffs and relocations to cheaper markets
Announced the review of the 5 percent VAT imposed on consumers consuming more than 50 units of electricity per month through the budget for the upcoming fiscal year.

Announced drafted regulations on the implementation of food sanitation, and safety education and training for food delivery workers. The draft act stipulates that new food delivery workers must complete at least an hour of food sanitation and safety training before they start working, and incumbent workers must also receive at least an hour of training each year.

Received the approval from the World Bank of a new five-year Country Partnership Framework alongside four development operations totaling USD 285 million to drive sustainable recovery, expand public service delivery, and stimulate job creation within a fragile, conflict-affected landscape. Strategically aligned with national stabilization priorities, the foundational investments target rapid rehabilitation across critical multi-sector networks including public health systems, nutrition programs, primary electrical grids, municipal water harvesting installations, and agricultural and fisheries management. By pivoting toward an agile, localized deployment model, the programmatic framework seeks to rebuild institutional capacities, enhance macroeconomic governance, and empower vulnerable populations by expanding the economic participation of women and scaling private sector infrastructure investments.

Croatia has unveiled a new (USD 54 million) package of financial instruments aimed at strengthening agriculture, food processing and rural development, offering farmers and producers access to loans and credits with principal write-offs of up to 50 percent.

The Republic of Moldova will receive 250 million dollars from the World Bank to strengthen competitiveness, job creation, market efficiency and transparency, as well as economic integration with the European Union. The support aims to help the Government increase resilience against future shocks and advance the country’s path to EU accession, complementing the EU Growth and Reform Plan for Moldova.

With direct bilateral procurement support from the People's Republic of China, launched a comprehensive precision agritech initiative in Qornayel to integrate advanced drone platforms into its national sector system. Structured under the framework of the ministry's strategic transformation masterplan, the modernization program deploys automated aerial hardware to run optimized, low-impact pesticide crop sprayings, manage vulnerable natural pollinator ecosystems, and establish continuous remote-sensing monitoring across rugged mountainous forests to combat volatile wildfire hazards and invasive biological blights. By capturing highly accurate spatial field data, the institutional framework aims to rationalize raw inputs such as water and fertilizers while establishing data-driven traceability and food safety tracking structures to elevate the trade competitiveness of national agrifood exports.

Announced two new localized agricultural investment projects in the Al Ghuwayl area of the Ibri Wilayat, situated within the Al Dhahirah Governorate. Part of a broader state-backed strategy to expand modern agricultural production through private sector capital, the first venture establishes an advanced 10-acre tissue culture laboratory designed for the rapid and large-scale cultivation of disease-free, high-quality botanical seedlings and saplings to supply the domestic farming market. The second concurrent project allocates an additional 10 acres to the intensive cultivation of leafy vegetables utilizing a combination of protected greenhouse environments and traditional open fields. By introducing advanced agricultural technologies such as controlled-environment greenhouse systems and automated resource-efficiency workflows, the integrated initiatives are engineered to maximize year-round crop yields, conserve local groundwater resources, and accelerate import substitution to fortify national food security architecture in line with Oman Vision 2040.

Launched a series of community-centric environmental preservation initiatives timed with World Environment Day. Structured to advance the UAE's strategic target of planting 100 million mangroves by 2030 and fulfilling its obligations under the international Mangrove Alliance for Climate (MAC), the multi-regional field operations encompassed a large-scale mangrove restoration drive at Khor Kalba, an endangered marine turtle release at the Jebel Ali Wildlife Sanctuary, and specialized public health workshops at the Thukher Club to embed food safety systems and sustainable consumption habits within family units. Backed by quantitative gains in national metrics—including elevating the domestic environmental awareness index to 89% and the environmental behavior index to 85% through volunteer-led tree distribution campaigns—these initiatives utilize nature-based carbon sequestration and public ecology programs to reinforce regional biodiversity protection and long-term climate change mitigation.

Officially launched the Abu Dhabi Water and Energy Resilience Framework. Structured around three foundational pillars—infrastructure, human capital and governance, and technology and innovation—the newly introduced framework mandates 15 strategic measures designed to optimize supply security, capacity planning, emergency preparedness, and the diversification of vital resource networks. Developed to align with the UAE Water Security Strategy 2036 and the Net Zero 2050 charter, the initiative integrates advanced reverse osmosis desalination technologies, artificial intelligence for meteorological forecasting, and cloud-seeding methodologies advanced by the National Centre of Meteorology. Multi-lateral collaborations emphasized treating water, energy, and food security as a single interconnected system.

Launched its 2026 wheat procurement season with an expected harvest of 2.5 million tons, aiming to strengthen domestic food security and reduce reliance on imports. The government is supporting farmers through Decree No. 120, offering a bonus of 9,000 Syrian pounds (about USD 70) per ton in addition to a procurement price of 46,000 pounds (about USD 380) per ton, while expanding storage capacity to nearly 1 million tons across 37 silos and 98 facilities and rehabilitating key infrastructure, including the Adra silos with a capacity of 200,000 tons. Efforts also include digital systems for delivery and registration, and regional production estimates such as 1.025 million tons from 750,000 hectares in Hasakah, all contributing to improved supply stability and long‑term food security.

Received the approval from the World Bank for a EUR 191.5 million (USD 219.4 million) loan to modernize urban infrastructure and services in the fast-growing cities of Antalya and Konya, addressing a growing demand for public transport, clean water and sanitation, and efficient energy systems, while generating jobs along the way.

Italian Minister of Economy and Finance and the Minister of Environment and Energy Security, temporarily reduces excise duties on selected transport fuels from 7 June to 3 July 2026. The measure is triggered by an increase in international crude oil prices during May 2026, which generated higher-than-expected VAT revenues. Under existing legislation, part of these additional VAT receipts is used to offset fuel costs by lowering excise taxes.

Hungary's government will stop issuing worker visas to employees from the Philippines, ‌Georgia and Armenia from Friday, a government ‌spokeswoman said, calling the move a first step towards regulating the ​inflow of guest workers.

Greece’s Parliament has approved a new Spatial Planning and Urban Development Code, consolidating more than 180 laws and regulations into a single framework. The reform is designed to simplify planning and building legislation while improving legal clarity and accessibility.

Announced that the more than 50 days worth fuel reserve has moved to the status of amber alert, which would ordinarily mean they had less that 30 days worth. This was done as a precautionary measure, and that there is no impending fuel shortage.

Announced the distribution of over 20 000 tractors to farmers in the next fiscal year under the Green Tractor Scheme in Punjab. The next phase of the Green Tractor Scheme will offer a subsidy of PKR 1.5 million (USD 5 300) on high-horsepower tractors and PKR 750 000 (USD 2 600) on tractors in the 50 to 65 horsepower range. Under the earlier phase of the scheme, the provincial government provided a subsidy of PKR 1 million (USD 3 500) on 9 500 high-horsepower tractors. It also announced that 10 000 tractors in the 50 to 65 horsepower range are being supplied to farmers with a subsidy of PKR 500 000 (USD 1 800) each.

Distributed insurance payments to individual and legal entities who participated to the press conference on the announcement of insurance payments. The total amount of payments will be 7,129,347 soms (USD 81,500), which will be distributed across the following types of insurance: i) Mandatory Motor Thid Party Liability Insurance (OSAGO); Auto CASCO; Accident insurance; other insurance products.

Granted land-use rights to more than 1.2 million people and is preparing a new initiative to resolve long-standing disputes that have persisted for more than six decades. The programme, implemented through the Office of the National Land Policy Board, aims to provide secure land-use rights for people living and farming on state-owned land while preserving forest resources.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Reshaped its climate funding strategy after winning the approval for reforms aimed at unlocking access to a new UN-backed fund with more than USD 731 million pledged by developed nations. The overhaul creates a dedicated climate agency, streamlines approval procedures and positions Thailand to compete for disaster recovery and adaptation funding as forecasters warn that a strengthening El Niño could raise the risk of droughts, heatwaves and severe weather across the region later this year.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Planned stricter regulation of health food marketing claims by limiting the functional terms that can be used for 17 designated ingredients or compounds and requiring manufacturers to register related products.

Signed a decree to levy a 0.5% tax on gross revenue from electricity exports to fund universal access to energy. The decree stipulates that 60% of the funds will be invested in projects outside the national electricity grid, through the Energy Fund and 40% in projects included in the national grid, under the responsibility of Electricidade de Mozambique.

Unveiled KSh 540 million (approximately USD 4.2 million) monthly conditional cash transfer (CCT) programme for unskilled youth. Under the National Youth Opportunities Towards Advancement (NYOTA) programme, 90,000 young Kenyans without formal qualifications will receive KSh 6,000 per month (approximately USD 46 per month) for six months, alongside full funding for vocational training and technical certification.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Announced the elimination of taxes on batteries and solar panels. This initiative aims to facilitate access to renewable energy for households, businesses, and institutions, while reducing dependence on traditional energy sources.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Launched a major initiative to place national and regional scientific research at the centre of policymaking, aiming to dismantle academic silos and better connect scientific work with public policy and community action.
Opened electricity system to private investments to address the collapse of a grid that has been battered by blackouts and problems over the past two decades, and includes a tariff increase.

Proposed a tax regime for the oild and gas sector that would deliver a breakeven price for extra-heavy oil of USD 27 per barrel. The fiscal framework proposed by the Venezuelan opposition is designed to revive the country's dilapidated oil and gas industry and increase oil output at least fourfold.
European Commission approves EUR 25 million (USD 28 million) Spanish State aid for fishing companies facing increased fuel prices.

New regulations and direct financial support will be provided to citizens who are working or seeking employment in the country and across the European Union. On June 4, the Parliament approved the draft law in its first reading, which aims to promote employment and unemployment insurance for Moldovans living abroad.

Distributed specialized agricultural equipment and maintenance tools to 22 farmers in the region, executing as a key component of the "Enhancing Land Productivity and Adapting to Climate Change through Afforestation" project, the logistics deployment provides essential hardware to smallholders who have successfully completed intensive land reclamation and planting phases. By delivering technical and material resources to rural and marginalized areas, the institutional framework aims to scale up soil efficiency, accelerate tree-planting initiatives, and lower operational overhead costs, thereby enabling farmers to sustainably manage and protect their newly reclaimed acreage against environmental degradation.
Announced that Türkiye’s new tax law will reduce the corporate tax rate from 25% to 12.5% for manufacturing and agricultural production sectors

Introduced a new personal tax regime that includes a 20-year exemption for certain foreign-sourced income of individuals becoming tax-resident in Turkiye on or after 1 January 2026, a reduced 1 percent inheritance and gift tax rate for qualifying inherited assets and an asset repatriation mechanism available until 31 July 2027. The foreign income exemption applies to individuals who have not had residence or tax liability in Turkiye during the prior three calendar years and whose income is derived from abroad, representing a significant policy shift that may enhance Turkiye's attractiveness for internationally mobile individuals, high-net-worth taxpayers and cross-border business activity.
Announced the establishment of a review mechanism to restrict imports of goods linked to forced labour, after the United States proposed imposing additional tariffs.

Launched a one-stop banking initative aimed at making it easier for foreign residents to access financial services, designateing six banks to provide streamline account opening, credit and international transfer services.

Adopted the Children’s Protection and Welfare (Amendment) Bill 2023, a significant step towards strengthening the protection of children’s rights and welfare in Lesotho. The amendment is expected to enhance child protection mechanisms and reinforce the country’s commitment to ensuring that every child enjoys their fundamental rights and reaches their full potential.

Formally Initiated the process to establish the institution, which will support the growth of small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and entrepreneurs through microcredit loans of up to GYD 3 million (approximately USD 14,400). The government has committed GYD 40 billion (USD 192 million) to the institution, with approximately GYD 20 billion (USD 96 million) already allocated in Budget 2026 ahead of its planned launch later this year.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: Released 85 percent of the approved 2026 budget to accelerate food production, strengthen agro-industrialization and improve food security.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: GEF granted a USD 77.6 million environmental finance package to support climate and nature projects across 10 countries. For Eritrea, the key item is a new GEF Trust Fund project aimed at restoring degraded land, placing the country within a wider international push to link climate resilience, biodiversity protection and sustainable livelihoods. UNDP listed Eritrea alongside Zimbabwe, Botswana, the Philippines, Malaysia, India and Kyrgyzstan among countries receiving support through new GEF Trust Fund projects.

Delivered instruments of accession to the Protocols of the Cape Town Convention on matters specific to Railway Rolling Stoc, Space Assets and Mining. Agricultural and Construction Equipment. Having already acceded to the Cape Town Convention itself, as well as the Protocol on matters specific to Aircraft Equipment, in 2016, the Democratic Republic of the Congo has become the second State to be a Party to all Protocols in the Cape Town Convention system. The Rail Protocol will become effective for the Democratic Republic of the Congo as of 1 October 2026, whereas the Space and MAC Protocols will enter into force when the requirements under their respective Articles XXXVIII(1) and XXV(1) have been satisfied.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Expanded mandatory consumption reporting requirements for large companies with the Energy Efficiency Law. The regulation requires companies to report their annual electricity and fuel consumption through the National Energy Balance. With this update, the universe of companies required to report is expanded to include medium-sized and commercial companies that, in many cases, have no prior experience in energy management.The regulations place special attention on the so-called Energy Management Capacity Consumers (CCGE), a category that includes companies with consumption above 50 Tcal (teracalories) per year, typical of large industrial facilities or companies with high energy intensity within the production system. Tcal are a unit of energy used to measure large-scale consumption. One Tcal is equivalent to one billion calories and is used to express a company’s total electricity and fuel consumption in a single indicator.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policy_description: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements
policydecision_details: Strengthened health requirements related to the use of antimicrobials in animal production with the Execution Regulation (EU) 2026/1189. The measure modifies Regulation (EU) 2021/405 and is part of the European food safety scheme based on the "One Health" approach, aimed at reducing antimicrobial resistance through stricter controls throughout the entire production chain. The new regime It establishes that third countries must demonstrate effective compliance. of European health standards, with special emphasis on product traceability and restrictions on the use of certain antimicrobials in animals intended for human consumption.
policycategory: Sanitary, phytosanitary and technical standards improvements

policydecision_details: Approved a revised budget of CFA 4 086.62 billion (USD 72 bullion), 8 percent higher than the original finance law. Authorities will direct additional resources toward social services, education, security, infrastructure and agriculture
