Issued the Executive Order N.44 to establish customs enforcements and other import-related provisions.
The European Commission has approved a EUR 54 million (USD 62 million) Spanish State aid scheme to support agricultural companies facing increased fuel prices due to the Middle East crisis.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: The Government has approved the Strategic Program for Agricultural Policy for 2026–2030, a document that sets out how subsidies will be granted to farmers and for the development of the agri-food sector over the next five years. The Program proposes a gradual increase in allocations for the sector, from 2.3 billion lei in 2026 to 5.3 billion lei in 2030, with a planned cumulative budget of 18.9 billion lei.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: Implemented Decree No. 289/202 to restrict the import of essential grains and agricultural raw materials, including wheat, maize, barley, and soybeans, exclusively to active domestic manufacturing and production units. Engineered to dismantle speculative market brokerage, artificial price manipulation, and hoarding by non-producing traders, the new state-backed framework strictly links allowed import volumes directly to the verified operational capacities of local agricultural and processing facilities. By introducing enhanced supply-chain monitoring, compliance oversight, and digital traceability systems, the policy has stabilized the distribution of foundational feed ingredients, resulting in a gradual correction of retail prices for meat, poultry, and eggs. This public asset intervention optimizes domestic value-chain efficiency and insulates household spending from market distortions, thereby advancing the state's long-term macro-level food security and economic stabilization objectives.

In collaboration with FAO, executed a specialized technical training program for 20 women from the Abu Dis Cooperative Society for Livestock Development. Funded through a broader West Bank animal value chain optimization framework, the capacity-building initiative delivers theoretical and practical instruction on public safety, rigorous sterilization protocols, and advanced livestock care methodologies. To enhance domestic marketing opportunities and maximize economic returns for smallholders, the curriculum introduces product diversification techniques—such as the manufacturing of specialized cheese varieties like mozzarella—alongside strategic farm management frameworks. By explicitly targeting the economic participation and technical literacy of rural women, the structural intervention drives production efficiency and scales up localized food safety standards to reinforce smallholder family livelihoods.

Announced the expansion of payment limitation and payment eligibility provisions that affect program payments including allowing for the equitable treatment of business entities. Additionally, producers will benefit from an increased payment limitation for certain programs, and a broader definition of farming income that will result in more exceptions to income limitations.
The new government of Denmark has taken a landmark decision to better protect public health by lowering the nitrate limit in drinking water, currently set at 50 milligrams per litre (mg/L) in the EU.
Longan farmers are expected to gain greater access to the Chinese market after Cambodia and China reached a protocol on sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) measures.

The Government of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina, passed a Decision adopting the Program for the expenditure of funds determined by the FBiH Budget for 2026 for the Program Improving the Socio-Economic Status of Members of the Veteran Population and Preservation of the Assets of the Defense and Liberation War, to this Ministry as part of ongoing transfers to non-profit organizations, in the amount of 1,720,000 KM (USD 1 million) .

Approved a new levy regime on selected grain and oilseed imports in a move aimed at protecting domestic producers from cheaper foreign competition, strengthening food security, and generating funding for climate-resilient agricultural infrastructure. The policy, which takes effect immediately under Statutory Instrument 87 of 2025, reflects a broader government strategy to promote import substitution, support local farmers, and reduce the country’s dependence on imported grain amid growing climate and foreign currency pressures.

Suspended temporarily the grants of 15 825 old-age pensions beneficiaries whose names could not be verified on the National Population Registry System. The verification process forms part of their efforts to maintain the accuracy of the social grants beneficiary list and is in line with verification measures used in social protection schemes

Establisehd subsidies for farmers in the cotton, rice, soybeans and cashew sectors from the 2026-2027 agricultural campaign to better reward productive effort, sustainably strengthen farmers' incomes, secure the supply of local processing units consolidate the conutry positioning in the region. For a national production exceeding 700 000 tons, producers will receive an additional premium of FCFA/kg 10 (USD/kg 0.176) on the approved price of the agricultural campaign. Concerning rice, cashew and soybeans, once installed processing capacities are satisfied, producers will received an additional premium of FCFA/kg 10 (USD/kg 0.17) per kilogra delivered to local factories.

Formalized its request to join the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), considered the fourth largest free trade area at global level, with 12 countries participating (Australia, Brunei, Canada, Chile, Japan, Malaysia, Mexico, New Zealand, Peru, Singapore, the United Kingdom, and Viet Nam)

Doubled the child nutrition allowance for Dalit children under five to Rs1,000 per month (about USD 7.5), increasing the programme allocation from Rs2.08 billion (around USD 16 million) to Rs3 billion (about USD 23 million).
Unveiled incentives, including grants of up to 40% for about 20 million in agriculture and livestock production, to boost productivity and make farming more profitable and attractive.

Proclamation adjusting certain metals tariffs to more effectively address national security threats, spur investment in American agriculture, housing, and manufacturing, and facilitate U.S. production of related products. The Proclamation adjusts the tariffs on agricultural equipment, like combines and harvesters, as well as certain other equipment, from 25 percent to 15 percent.

The Council of Ministers has reinforced the financing of the autonomous communities and local authorities through a royal decree law that includes two key measures. Firstly, the advance payments corresponding to 2026 are updated. Secondly, local authorities with a budget surplus in 2025 are allowed to dedicate it to financially sustainable investments.

policy_description: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
policydecision_details: Romania’s state-controlled natural gas group Romgaz (BVB: SNG) announced that it signed on May 28 the contract to take over from Swiss Ameropa the productive assets of the country’s largest and sole functional fertilisers producer, Azomureş, for EUR 46.5 million plus corrections that may bring the final price to EUR 69 million.
policycategory: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs

policydecision_details: Enacted a comprehensive package of regulatory facilitation measures by amending the Executive Regulations of the Customs Law to accelerate cross-border trade flows. Under the new state-backed framework, maritime cargo handlers and commercial operators are permitted to initiate formal customs declarations immediately upon a vessel's arrival at national ports using only the bill of lading issued in the importer's name. This policy effectively decouples the initial declaration stage from the immediate submission of a delivery order, which can now be finalized at a later phase prior to the cargo's definitive release. Developed through technical consultations with the Ministry of Transport, regional shipping chambers, and commercial logistics agencies, the structural reform is engineered to shorten port clearance times, lower administrative overhead, and compress logistics performance index deficits while maintaining strict regulatory oversight to safeguard public

Temporarily reinstated a 170% import tariff on soft wheat and its derivatives, ending a multi-year tax exemption policy that has been in place since November 2021 to counter severe climate-driven droughts and volatile global commodity pricing. This protective trade mechanism is activated in response to an exceptional recovery in domestic agricultural yields, with national cereal production projected to surge to approximately 90 million quintals following improved rainfall patterns across major agricultural basins. This regulatory intervention is engineered to incentivize domestic millers and grain processors to prioritize purchasing from Moroccan smallholders. By establishing a robust trade barrier against cheaper foreign agricultural imports, the temporary policy aims to protect domestic rural incomes and stabilize the national grain market before transitioning back to a zero-rate import framework later in the year.

Launched a specialized multi-day technical training course at the AFDC Center in Ramlieh, Aley District. The technical program aims to train agricultural engineers, technicians, and military personnel on the operation, maintenance, and flight logistics of advanced agricultural drones donated by the People's Republic of China. This bilateral technology transfer establishes a digital monitoring and surveillance infrastructure across Lebanon's dense woodlands and agricultural zones, optimizing early detection vectors for crop diseases and invasive forest pests—particularly affecting cedar and pine ecosystems. By replacing traditional, high-risk ground applications with precision drone-based aerial mapping and localized pesticide spraying, the inter-institutional partnership lowers operational deployment costs, enhances spatial data accuracy, and accelerates environmental disaster response times.

Officially launched construction on a 65-square-kilometer, USD 4.2 billion sustainable agricultural city near Saham in the Al Batinah North region. Supervised by the infrastructure consultancy Surbana Jurong Group, the mega-project aims to aggressively mitigate import reliance—which currently drives 30% of national market purchases—by integrating high-efficiency agritech systems, including hydroponics, aeroponics, and advanced aquaculture networks designed to secure baseline nutrition for 25,000 residents annually. Operating as a structural anchor under the national food sufficiency strategy, which encompasses roughly 140 parallel development projects to buffer global supply chain volatility, the development model leverages subsidized hardware allocations and free land distributions to scale localized farming outputs and reinforce climate-resilient economic diversification.
Issued a military order to seize 30 hectares (74 acres) of Palestinian land near Bethlehem in the occupied West Bank under the pretext of expropriation for public purposes,

Greece is starting to implement a labor import deal with Egypt, signed in November 2022, amid a worsening demographic crisis. Highlighting the labor shortages in rural Greece, which have intensified year after year, the state-run AMNA news agency announced that the deal is finally moving toward implementation.

France’s National Assembly on Tuesday adopted an emergency agriculture bill that would make it easier to build water storage for irrigation, tighten controls on food imports and simplify a range of farming rules, in a move lawmakers said was meant to protect farm production and strengthen the country’s agricultural sovereignty.

Denmark's new coalition government unveiled its policy agenda Tuesday, focusing on taxes, expanded welfare measures and tighter social media regulations for children. The government plans to abolish the top-top and middle tax, leaving a basic tax rate for annual incomes up to 777,900 Danish kroner (USD 121,157) and a 15 percent top tax on income above that level.
The government announced a series of tougher measures aimed at containing the livestock disease outbreak that has shaken Cyprus' farming community and sparked protests by livestock breeders.
The State Council, China's cabinet, has issued a plan to accelerate agricultural and rural modernization during the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) period.

Russia will introduce temporary restrictions on imports of fresh sweet cherries, sour cherries, apricots, plums, peaches, nectarines and grape from Armenia starting June 2, 2026, said the Russian Federal Service for Veterinary and Phytosanitary Supervision.

Received a USD 6 million investment from GEF to implement the project Ridge to Reef Ecosystem Restoration in Solomon Islands. From watershed forests to riparian and coastal areas, the project will bring more than 45,000 hectares of land and other ecosystems under restoration, while improving the management of over 155,00 landscapes and marine habitats. Various threatened and native species will benefit, including plants, birds, bats, skinks, corals, cetaceans, dugongs, turtles, fish and sharks. A national ecosystem restoration policy will be developed and a variety of stakeholders will be involved at national, provincial and project site levels, ensuring local livelihoods and community resilience are supported.

Approved the import of 80 000 tons of fertilizer (60 000 tonnes of urea and 20 000 tonnes of DAP), but opened a letter of credit to import up to 50 000 tonnes of chemical fertilizers from India under a Government-to-government agreement. The first reason is the availability of financial resources and the second is the decline in prices in the global market.
Announced additional tariffs of up to 12.5 percent from 60 countries, subject to a public comment period ending on 6 July, following by public earing on 7 July.

Launched a nationwide project to digitize more than 10.5 million social security records and integrate them into its future E-Social Security Platform. Authorities expect the digital transformation to improve administrative efficiency, strengthen financial oversight and support the long-term sustainability of the pension system.

Signed a Free Trade Agreement with Peru. The FTA was initially signed on December 6, 2011, while the update document negotiated in 2014 was initialed on April 23, 2025. The ratification by Peru was made official on May 26, 2026, with the signing of Supreme Decree N°023-2026-RE.

Announced a new policy scheme according to which rice importers can no longer secure permits without first showing verifiable partnerships with Ghanaian rice producers, by investing in country's own rice farms and mills.

Enacted a law requiring the cattle industry to trace livestock and prove beef supply chains are free from deforestation. The law requires government agencies and private companies to integrate cattle-tracking, land ownership and deforestation-monitoring systems to identify livestock linked to forest loss and keep them out of supply chains.

Formalized the repeal of more than a dozen commercial and industry rules. The headline targets are three pillars: the Supply Law, the Shelf Law, adn the Price Observatory (all instrument from the oil price control system).

The Health Promotion Board will conduct regular checks to ensure accurate labeling. It requests the beverages such as coconut water that exceed sugar content thresholds must display Nutri-Grade labels rated “C” or “D,” with non-compliance constituting an offence.
Raised the small business tax transition threshold to 5 billion soums (about USD 400,000) to curb revenue misreporting and support enterprise growth.

Offered youth concessional loans of up to 100 million soums (about USD 8,000) under the “Youth Business” programme to support entrepreneurship and employment, with extended repayment and grace periods, one year for principal payments and up to three months for interest payments .
Considered tax cuts and subsidies to boost electric vehicle uptake, including incentives of up to 70,000 baht (about USD 2,145) for up to 150,000 vehicles, depending on type and model.
The programme has spent about 1,084 million baht, with 5 million users participating across over 566,000 shops, out of more than 26 million approved beneficiaries.

Unveiled a new stimulus package for the second half of 2026 to boost consumer spending and support labor markets. Announced by Coordinating Minister for Economic Affairs, the package includes tax cuts aligned with President campaign pledge.

Announced the implementation of new functionality for Employee Credit Program (Program) transactions. The new functionality allows employees to offer, inter alia, severance-related guarantees in Employee Credit Program transactions. The guarantees may include 35% of severance amounts, up to 10% of the Brazilian Severance Indemnity Fund (FGTS) balance and up to 100% of the FGTS termination fine. Employers should be prepared for related payroll, termination and eSocial / FGTS Digital processes.

Published in Argentina’s Official Gazette the Executive Orderd No. 407/2026 containing regulations for various provisions of the Employment Contract Law No. 20,744 (LCT), as amended by the Labor Modernization Act No. 27,802, in addition to regulations governing collective bargaining (Law No. 14,250), trade union organizations (Law No. 23,551), temporary staffing agencies (TSA), and construction industry registration (Law No. 22,250). The Order took effect on the date of its publication.

The European Investment Bank (EIB), part of the EIB Group, and the Government of the Autonomous Community of the Basque Country today signed the first EUR 250 million (USD 285 million) tranche of a loan approved for a total value of €500 million to modernise and expand healthcare infrastructure in the Basque Country in Spain.

Authorized the release of 21 imported veterinary products for local distribution following rigorous quality and compliance inspections. The approved batch includes 12 veterinary pharmaceuticals, 7 vaccines, and 2 additional medicinal substances, all of which met the strict technical and sanitary criteria enforced by the Veterinary Health Authority. This regulatory oversight ensures the availability of safe and effective animal health treatments to support domestic livestock breeders and bolster national food security.

Distributed financial grants totaling ILS 620,000 (USD 183,000) to 280 beneficiaries across the Ramallah, Al-Bireh, and Jerusalem governorates. Funded by the Danish government, this distribution initiates the first phase of a broader ILS 4.4 million (USD 1.30 million) Field and Fodder Crops Development Project designed to cultivate approximately 7,750 dunams of land and support 1,550 young farmers aged 19 to 29. By providing targeted capital to expand the localized production base of essential staples—including wheat, barley, lentils, vetch, broad beans, and chickpeas—the structural intervention aims to absorb displaced workforces affected by severe economic crises, scale up land utilization rates, and build sustainable rural livelihoods to reinforce national food security.

Prepared a dual support package for its high-tech sector, combining direct startup grants with a novel corporate tax mechanism that would allow multinational firms to pay taxes in U.S. dollars, Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich announced this week. The initiative addresses mounting pressure on Israel’s largest exporters, whose profitability has eroded as the shekel strengthened to historic highs against the dollar.
Announced the decision of designating five forests in ecologically sensitive zones are scheduled to be declared as reserves, raising Sri Lanka’s total number of forest reserves to 86.

Launched a joint initiative to restore inland fisheries livelihoods and strengthen the resilience of cyclone-affected fishing communities in Sri Lanka’s Eastern Province in partnership with Japan and FAO. Funded by the Government of Japan with a total budget of USD 1.33 million, the project will be implemented from June 2026 to November 2027 across Ampara, Batticaloa and Trincomalee districts, supporting fishers and Culture-Based Fisheries Organizations (CBFOs) affected by Cyclone Ditwah.

The Facilitation Committee, chaired by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, today approved the establishment of a EUR 200 million (USD 229 million) section of the 394/81 Fund dedicated to companies intending to invest in artificial intelligence.

Since 1 June 2026, exporters of designated strategic natural resources, currently comprising of coal, palm oil, and ferro alloys, have been subject to a centralised export framework under Government Regulation No. 24 of 2026 on the Governance of Exports of Strategic Natural Resource Commodities ("GR 24/2026"). Under the new framework, exports of these commodities are to be conducted through appointed state-owned enterprises ("Export SOEs") by no later than 31 December 2026, with the possibility that this deadline may be brought forward following a government evaluation.

policy_description: Tax on inputs or fixed capital
policydecision_details: Announced a reduction from 25 to 15 percent on tariffs on combines, bulldozers, mobile forklifts, cooling and heating equipments in recognition of the harm tariff inflict on American farmers by increasing the cost of agricultural equipment.
policycategory: Tax on inputs or fixed capital

policydecision_details: om 1 June 2026, China will implement a new regulatory framework governing the registration of overseas food production, processing, and storage facilities for food exported to the country. Issued under Decree No. 280 by the General Administration of Customs of the People’s Republic of China (GACC), the framework introduces a strengthened and risk-based registration system designed to enhance food safety oversight and tighten control over imported food supply chains.

Announced amendments to income tax, sales tax, federal excise duty and custom laws, with a focus on compliance, documentation and administrative changes, including increased use of digitial for reporting and monitoring. he Bill includes changes to individual taxation, including revised tax slabs (i.e., income/tax brackets) (0 percent up to PKR 600,000 (USD 2 100) and 35 percent above PKR 7 million (USD 24 600)), removal of the surcharge on salary income, and withdrawal of the deemed income provisions, alongside revisions to the super tax for higher-income taxpayers and certain sectors.
Adopted a policy of snatiching away the subsidies that cooperatives of tumeric farmers had been receiving in the past.
Became the first South Asian country to mandate a 15-day salary cycle.

Approved in principle an agreement with the Republic of Albania, concerning the establishment of joint border crossing points and integrated border control producers. The agreement aims to create shared border crossings between the two countries. It also introduces coordinated border control procedures. These measures are designed to facilitate the movement of citizens and goods. They also aim to strengthen cross-border cooperation.

Announced the installation and operationalization of a full container scanner at the Maldives’ main port within the next four months as part of efforts to strengthen border security and curb the illegal importation of goods, including narcotics and prohibited products.
Required employers with 10 or more employees to contribute to Thailand new's Employee Welfare Fund, introducing additional payroll, reporting, and compliance requirements.

Several local governments are running cash relief programs, while a national cash distribution (NTD 10 000/person, USD 136/person) is under government review. In Penghu County’s Huxi Township, residents will receive NTD 5 000 (USD 68) by 30 June . In nearby Xiyu Township, payments of NTD 10 000 (USD 136) run from June 2 to July 31. In Hualien County’s Fuli Township, residents receiving NT$3,000 from May 19 to July 2. In Guangfu Township, disaster-affected residents are eligible for NTD10 000 (USD 136), with payments made by bank transfer. In Miaoli County’s Tongluo Township, eligible residents will receive NTD 8 500 (USD , with cash distributions. In Nantou County’s Renai Township, eligible residents and qualifying newborns will receive NTD 2 000 (USD 30). In Taitung County’s Donghe Township, eligible residents will receive NTD 3 000 (USD 40). In Changhua County’s Huatan Township, residents are eligible for NTD 6 000 (USD . However, distribution has been delayed, with new dates to be announced by local authorities.

Approved a new grain procurement and import verification framework designed to create a transparent, accountable system that prioritises local farmers while ensuring agro-processors continue to access grain supplies in an orderly and efficient manner. The framework introduces a structured, market-based system that links grain import eligibility to verified local grain procurement via a transparent, digitally monitored platform. The framework is operationalising Statutory Instrument (SI) 87 of 2025 (CAP. 18:24) Agricultural Marketing Authority (Grain, Oilseed and Products) (Amendment) Regulations (No. 2), enacted by the Government last year to govern the import of grains and oilseed products as well as encourage local production

Launched the Payment System Vision (2028), a strategic framework designed to guide the development of Nigeria's payment ecosystem over the next several years. The initiative seeks to reduce delays, minimise transaction failures, and improve the efficiency of domestic and cross-border payment systems.

Extended the enforcement deadlined for the new Manufacturer and Exporter Registry. For each shipment, the Manifestación de Valor Electrónica (MVE) customs value declaration requires importers to electronically file a commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin, proof of payment, insurance documentation and Carta Porte (bill of lading and legal proof of possession). All must be cross-referenced for consistency and uploaded to a Mexican government portal. Any discrepancy between invoice and bill of lading triggers a fine. And without a proper MVE, the shipment doesn’t move.

Cut diesel prices to GMD115 (USD 1.58) per litre through a subsidy intervention worth GMD150 million (USD 3.7 million). he move is part of ongoing efforts to shield households, transport operators, and businesses from the impact of volatile global fuel markets. Petrol prices remain unchanged at D112 (USD 1.48) per litre.

Abolished the 100 percent tariff imposed on Colombian imports. The measure came into effect following a resolution issued by Ecuador's customs authority, which reduced the security surcharge on Colombian goods to zero. Officials described the decision as an opportunity to rebuild cooperation in trade, security and economic development.
Decreased diese prices by BRL 0.35 per litre (USD 0.07), after the government introduced a BRL 1.12 per litre (USD 0.22) subsidy.

Implemented the Brazil Sovereign Plan (Plano Brasil Soberano), reducing the minimum required revenue impact from 5 percent to 1 percent. With this measure, exporting companies and suppliers affected by US tariffs or by the economic impacts of conflicts in the Middle East will be able to access financing even if they experience smaller revenue losses. To access the credit, companies in these groups must demonstrate that exports accounted for at least 1 percent of their gross revenue during the reference period. Previously, the threshold was 5 percent. For Group 1 (impacted by US import tariffs), revenue losses must be compared with the 12-month period from July 1, 2024, to June 30, 2025. For Group 3 (impacted by Middle East conflict), revenue losses must be compared with the 12-month period from January 1, 2025, to December 31, 2025.

Announced modifications to custom duty and VAT rates applicable to certain imported products including nuts, (HS 08) and synthetic filament yarn (HS 54). The changes form part of the government's ongoing efforts to update customs procedures, improve tax administration, and align import regulations with current economic and trade policy objectives.

Published Executive Order No. 407/2026 implementing regulations for various provisions of the Employment Contract Law No 20,774, in addition to regulations governing collective bargaining, trade unions, temporary staffing agencies and construction industry registration. The order includes: mandatory employment registration, pay slip, fringe benefits and in-kind compensation, illness monitoring and medical certificates.

The French government has announced a mid-year increase in the national minimum wage (SMIC), boosting it by 2.41 percent in response to persistent inflationary pressures. The new rate takes effect on June 1, 2026, and will automatically raise salary thresholds for several key immigration and work visa categories.

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: Sri Lanka’s fuel subsidy allocation of Rs57 billion (USD 195 million) will end by June, even as prices remain below cost, with temporary accommodation by the IMF.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: Planned to tighten fuel quotas as the CPC’s import bill reached USD 524 million in May, reflecting rising foreign exchange pressures amid efforts to curb fuel consumption during the ongoing economic crisis.

Introduced a new prudential levy on banks, insurers, and other financial institutions, shifting the cost of regulation to the financial industry and aligning with the funding approach of the Financial Markets Authority and the Commerce Commission.
Enacted the revised expatriate salary policy.

policy_description: Unspecified production support|Ecosystem and habitat preservation
policydecision_details: Launched a national programme through 2030 to support sustainable business practices, targeting 25,000 enterprises and the development of at least 20 scalable pilot models.
policycategory: Unspecified production support|Ecosystem and habitat preservation

policydecision_details: Enforced stricter food safety rules for kindergartens, including bans on high-risk foods, tighter limits on additives, and requirements that suppliers have no food safety violations in the past three year
Planned “one-gate” export system, centralized under Danantara Sumberdaya Indonesia (DSI), is raising monopoly concerns.

Enacted the “Administrative Measures for the Registration of Overseas Food Production Enterprises Importing Food into China” (GACC Decree No. 280), issued on 14 October 2025. The new regulations require all foreign food exporters to comply with updated procedures, although most businesses are already largely compliant. The measures aim to strengthen the safety of imported food and support the long-term sustainability of international food trade.

Opened the registration for the “Thais Help Thais Plus” programme to up to 30 million people, offering a 60/40 co-payment scheme in which the government subsidizes 60% of eligible spending. The support covers food, beverages, goods, and selected services purchased from participating businesses.

More protection for bees and other pollinators, such as wasps and butterflies, and the planting of new trees. These are two of the innovations provided for in Legislative Decree 80/2026, in force since 31 May 2026, for the protection of nature, which adapts national legislation to the provisions of EU Regulation 2024/1991.

Bangladesh–US Cotton Trade Agreement is under negotiation. The US cotton initiative identifies Bangladesh as a key market, with plans to boost American cotton exports. Bangladesh may benefit from tariff reductions on apparel made with US cotton and textile inputs, along with additional trade concessions.
decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: Extended measures aimed at limiting fuel price increase for an additional two months. For diesel, the government will maintain a subsidy of 1.12 reais (USD 0.22) per liter for domestic refiners and fuel importers beginning June 1. Officials said two subsidy programs introduced in April will be merged into a single mechanism intended to support price stability.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: Banned single-use plastic water bottles in state institutions, directing government agencies to stop their use and take immediate steps to eliminate single-use plastics.
Planned to introduce a “Blue Lane” customs clearance system for authorized businesses to streamline trade and expedite processing.
Japan is preparing a supplementary budget of about ¥3 trillion (around $19 billion) to ease living costs amid high energy prices and a weak yen, while keeping 2026 bond issuance unchanged.

Committed USD 3.8 billion to nature as critical infrastructure: The government’s new strategy, A Force of Nature, aims to restore habitats, align industrial and conservation efforts, and mobilize investment for nature protection. Expected outcomes of Canada’s A Force of Nature strategy include: Restored ecosystems and critical habitats, improving biodiversity and resilience Better alignment of industrial activity with conservation goals, reducing environmental impacts Increased public and private investment in nature, including new financing mechanisms Enhanced climate resilience, such as carbon sequestration and natural disaster mitigation Stronger protection of natural areas, contributing to national and global conservation targets
Gazzetted the Water Skiing and Motor Boat control Bill 2026, containing amendments on the application areas and on the speed limits.
Gazzetted the Value Added Tax 2026, contains amendments on the application of VAT.

Classified 14 minerals as critical, banning the export of all raw or unbeneficiated forms, and mandated state shareholding through special-purpose vehicles, a long-awaited codification of industrial policy that follows a dramatic surge in lithium revenue.
Unveiled reforms to modernize its capital market, including introducing intraday trading, with the aim of creating a more dynamic, technology-driven, and globally competitive financial system.
Japan’s parliament has passed a bill to strengthen oversight of foreign investments, with the upper house approving revisions to the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act.

Expanded monitoring requirements to includ plastic containers , glass bottles, aluminium casks, and papaer cartons used in food and beverages packaging. Specific tariff codes (es. 3915.10.00.00, 3923.30.91.00, 4811.59.20.00) are now clearly defined to ensure stricter control and compliance. This update reflects a broader effort to modernize sanitary surveillance and strengthen food safety standards across all packaging materials in commercial distribution.

Distributed over 1.9 million bags of fertilizers to nearly one million farmers, as a part of efforts to boost agricultural productivity and strengthen food security nationwide. Fertiliser distribution was complemented by 12,000 litres of organic fertiliser, while 109 fertiliser inspectors and 329 industry stakeholders were trained on regulatory compliance to curb fake agricultural inputs.
Formalized preferential tariffs on selected Taiwanese exports, capping Section 232 tariffs at 15% for certain auto parts, timber, and wood products
decision_making_institution: Government of Taiwan Province of China

policydecision_details: Announced the doubling of the lowest tax slab to NPR 10 lakh (approximately USD 6,550) and slashed the top rate by 10 percentage points. The amendments merged the separate single and couple schedules into one, raised the first 1 percent band from NPR 500 000 (USD 3 280) to NPR 1 000 000 (USD 6 550), and cut the maximum rate from 39 percent to 29 percent.

policy_description: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
policydecision_details: Launched a Section 301 investigation concluding that certain acts, policies and practices of Brazil are unreasonable or discriminatory and burden or restrict US commerce, and proposed tariffs of 25% on Brazilian goods, subject to specified exemptions.
policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures

policydecision_details: Announced a series of trade defense measures, including actions aimed at the steel industry, as well as expanded support for exporters. The agency approved the inclusion of carbon steel bars on the list of products subject to temporary tariff increases due to temporary trade imbalances, raising the number of covered items to 20. The measure meets a request from Aço Brasil (IABr), which represents Brazil’s steelmakers.
Signed an agreement with Viet Nam have to commit the open and uninterrupted trade flows, ensuring the continued operation of key transport and trade infrastructure to minimize disruptions.

Nepal’s government has reduced the overall agricultural budget 2026/2027, despite increasing fertilizer allocations to Rs28.82 billion (about USD 215–220 million), while committing to introduce a fertilizer supply calendar.

policy_description: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: Nepal’s 2026–27 budget, presented on May 29 under Prime Minister Balendra Shah, comes at a critical economic turning point, with strong public expectations and a stable government. It allocates Rs3.63 billion to the labour sector, focusing on safer foreign employment, skills development, and measures such as zero-cost migration and remittance investment schemes.
policycategory: Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: Kazakhstan and Russia have reached a financial agreement for a 2.4 GW nuclear power project, featuring two VVER‑1200 Generation III+ reactors and an estimated cost of about USD 16.5 billion. Major construction is expected to begin in 2027.

Launched a Greenhouse Crop Insurance product aimed at protecting farmers against losses and boosting investment in climate smart-agriculture. The insurance product was unveiled during an event held at the headquarters of the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda (NISR), bringing together 123 farmers from all districts of the country, representatives from insurance companies, and senior officials from the Ministry of Agriculture and Animal Resources (MINAGRI), the Rwanda Agriculture and Animal Resources Development Board (RAB), and the National Agricultural Export Development Board (NAEB).

On May 4, 2026, the Netherlands issued Regulation of the Minister of Health, Welfare and Sport of April 23, 2026 (reference 4375777-1097324-WJZ), amending the requirements for food contact ceramics under the Commodities Act (Regulation on Packaging and Consumer Products) (‘the Regulation’). This revision is related to the Decision of the Benelux Committee of Ministers concerning ceramic articles intended to come into contact with food. The new law will become effective on May 29, 2026.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Launched a consultation on its Renewable Energy Strategy to 2035, targeting 22–26 GW of installed capacity and aiming for renewables to account for 35%–40% of the power mix.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Launched its most systematic push yet against foreign nominee land structures. The 2026 measures cover everything from a national corporate land registry to standardised investigation checklists and provincial monitoring committees across eight priority provinces: Phuket, Surat Thani, Mae Hong Son, Chiang Mai, Krabi, Chon Buri, Rayong, and Chanthaburi.

Poland has introduced a temporary ban on imports of fruits and vegetables containing traces of four pesticides prohibited in the EU, aiming to prompt action from the European Commission at the EU level.
Announced reformes against cattle rustling to protect small producers.

The USDA has announced over USD 9.75 million in funding through the Acer and Micro-Grants for Food Security programs to support the maple syrup industry and strengthen local food production in food-insecure communities. Eligible applicants are agricultural agencies, commissions, or departments in Alaska, American Samoa, the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, the Federated States of Micronesia, Guam, Hawaii, the Republic of the Marshall Islands, the Republic of Palau, and the United States Virgin Islands.
decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

policy_description: Animal health measures|Livestock measures and regulations
policydecision_details: Adopted a joint 2026-2028 Action Plan with South Africa aimed at strengthen regional cooperation in the fight against Foot and Mouth Disease. The action plan includes coordinated vaccination campaigns, maintenance of border fences, strengthening of diagnostic capacity and joint livestock farmer training programmes in key border regions such as Lobatse-Mahikeng and Francistown-Musina.
policycategory: Animal health measures|Livestock measures and regulations

policydecision_details: Confirmed that the New World screwworm is not present domestically but remains a growing threat, prompting livestock import restrictions from Mexico and heightened surveillance. Authorities have launched a multi‑agency response, including emergency drug authorizations and containment measures, to prevent outbreaks and limit potential economic losses exceeding USD 2 billion.
decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

policydecision_details: Launched a reform of its forestry and water management service as it is grappling with mounting environmental and climate-related risks. The proposed legislation calls for a broad modernisation of the service aimed at improving its operational effectiveness, nationwide reach, and monitoring and response capabilities. The reform would also expand the service’s responsibilities in areas including sustainable forest resource management, protected area conservation, reforestation, law enforcement, and public awareness campaigns.

Piloted part-time employment system. The initiative has launched in Thimphu, attracting about 130 job seekers, with up to 50 companies set to participate under the Department of Employment and Entrepreneurship.

policy_description: Seed technology and quality assurance systems
policydecision_details: Announed two major strategic framrworks designed to transform its seed industru over the next five year (the National Seed Sector Development Plan, the National Seed System Investment Plan) both covering the period 2026-2030.
policycategory: Seed technology and quality assurance systems

policydecision_details: Enacted the Credit Reference Act 2025, aimed at strengthenining the country's financial system and improving access to credit. The Bill seeks to repeal and replace the Credit Reference Act of 2011. It provides a legal framework for the establishment and regulation of credit reference bureaus, sets conditions for credit reporting, and addresses other related financial matters.

Allowed microfinance institutions to offer factoring services, with a reform aiming to improve financing access for small businesses. Factoring allows a company to receive immediate cash by selling unpaid invoices to a financial institution.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures|Water policies and regulations
policydecision_details: Introduced a Senate bill to redefine Puerto Rico's Maritime-Terrestrial Zone to reflect sea-leve rise and other climate risks not addressed under current law, that defines the Maritime-Terrestrial Zone as the coastal area affected by tides and storm waves, including reclaimed lands and riverbanks up to navigable or tidal points. The bill argues that the existing framework no longer reflects Puerto Rico’s “present climate reality” because it does not adequately address rising sea levels, coastal erosion or the protection of coastal ecosystems and public access.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures|Water policies and regulations

policydecision_details: Signed into a law a measure that eliminates 6 percent tax previously levied on airlines tickets. The policy shift could help reveive struggling cotton sector and support biofuel investments led by Italian oil company Eni.

policydecision_details: Authorised farmers in an emergency area to use tax credit certifiates from the General Tax Directorate to purchase diesel. Decree No. 77/026 allows the assignment of these credits exclusively for fuel purchases from authorized service stations and distributors, capped at 10% of diesel purchases made between March and May of 2025.

Approved the regulation for the IBS and the Goods and Services Contribution which will serve as an operational manual for the new dual VAT, marking a significant step forward in the implementation of the Brazilian Tax Reform.

Introduced amendments to the Insurance and Pensions Commisions Act, to ensure that these industries are aligned with global best practices. As the regulatory landscape evolves globally and domestically, it is essential for IPEC to stay aligned with emerging trends and best practices. These changes aim to strengthen the regulatory framework overseeing Zimbabwe’s insurance and pensions sectors. The amendments have far-reaching implications for insurers, pension funds, asset managers, and medical aid societies and the National Social Security Authority (NSSA).

Approved the management and functional review of five key democratic institutions, including the Electoral Commission for Sierra Leone and the Sierra Leone Broadcasting corporation. These reviews are intended to improve institutional efficiency, accountability and transparency.

Seven local governments in regional Western Australia will share over AUD 630,000 (approximately USD 410,000) under the Community Water Supplies Partnership program to fund water infrastructure projects that improve water security, firefighting capacity, and climate resilience.

Announced the start of a comprehensive and orderly process for restructuring sovreignity and state oil company debt, with the intention to put the economy at the service of the Venezuelan people and free the country from the burden of accumulated debt.

Announced the Plán Mexico actions aiming at accelerating productive investments and strengthening Mexico's position, including i) broad regulatory simplification measures, ii) faster permitting timelines for priority projects; iii) new centralized investments oversight mechanisms; iv) forthcoming single window foreign trade platform to digitize and streamline producers.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Indonesia is accelerating its clean energy transition with plans to develop up to 100 GW of solar capacity, making it a central pillar of its long-term strategy, alongside expanded electrification and alternative fuel initiatives.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: On May 14, Hungary lost the validity of Resolution 130/2023, which banned the import of more than 20 categories of Ukrainian agricultural products from 2023 – grain, oilseeds, flour, poultry meat, eggs, etc. The resolution was an emergency decree, and the new Hungarian government ended the state of emergency on May 13.

Launched a new National Cooperative Policy aimed at revitalising the country’s cooperative sector and strengthening its role in agriculture, food security and rural development. The policy places strong emphasis on agriculture, which remains central to The Gambia’s economy and employment.

policy_description: Import ban|Government procurement from domestic farmers
policydecision_details: Suspended maize imports to safeguard local production and food sovereignity. This shift in policy comes after reports surfaced that domestic producers are constantly battling to sell massive stockpiles of harvested maize, even as authorized imports continue to saturate the market. To ensure these surplus stocks are absorbed, the government is mobilizing specialized agencies like the Grain Board (Office Céréalier) and private sector partners to purchase and store the maize. Furthermore, the administration plans to coordinate with the poultry sector—a major consumer of maize—by regulating the import of day-old chicks and hatching eggs. By stimulating demand within the local livestock industry, the government aims to clear the “stranded” stocks and provide immediate financial relief to rural producers.
policycategory: Import ban|Government procurement from domestic farmers

policydecision_details: The government, through its annual policies and programmes, has announced plans to promote Nepal as a technology hub, unveiling measures to expand IT exports, digital infrastructure, and technology-based employment.

The import process at the Bhairahawa border, which had become difficult due to the mandatory requirement to mention the Maximum Retail Price (MRP) at the customs point, has started easing following facilitation measures introduced by the Department of Customs.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: The French Development Agency will provide the Republic of Moldova with a loan of EUR 45 million (USD 52 million) and a grant of EUR 11.2 million (USD 13 million) to rehabilitate the centralized irrigation systems in Călinești, Fălești district, and Criulenii de Sus, Criuleni district.

EU rules that update the lists of pollutants in surface and groundwaters have entered into force, aiming to improve water resilience and reduce pollution. The updated lists reflect the latest scientific advice and ensure that new substances are monitored more closely and subject to stricter controls.
Fixed the minimum purchase price of maize at CFA 1 700 per kg in a move to protect farmers from exploitative buying practices during the harvest season.

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations

policydecision_details: Enforced strict alcohol import limits: non‑Muslim travelers over 17 may bring in up to 2 bottles of liquor (about 2 litres) and 12 cans of beer per person, with undeclared or excess amounts subject to confiscation and fines.

In FY2025–26, the government allocated BDT 90.25 billion (about USD 820 million) for export incentives and is considering doubling the source tax on these payments in the upcoming budget to boost revenue amid pressure on exporters.
Reaffirmed that its new export quota for lithium are more than sufficient to sustain mining operations until the full ban on raw concentrate export in 2027.

The Swedish Ministry of Finance has submitted a draft bill (memorandum Fi2026/01131, published 13 May 2026) proposing a further temporary reduction of tax on petrol and diesel in response to rising fuel prices. The proposal would reduce the carbon dioxide tax on petrol and diesel by SEK 2.40 per litre for the period 1 July to 30 November 2026.

Planned to invest more than RWF 1.3 billion (USD 890 000) in cold storage and produce-processing infrastructure aimed at reducing post-harvest losses and strengthening the country's agricultural exports. The investment is part of the government’s “Export Logistics Development” project, which seeks to improve Rwanda’s capacity to store, process and transport agricultural and livestock products to international markets without compromising quality.

Ordered all opertators without valid mining permits or those that have failed to comply with their legal obligations to immediately stop activities and dismantle their gold processing facilities. The statement warns that companies failing to comply will face forced dismantling operations carried out by administrative authorities with support from security forces. The costs of those interventions would then be charged to the operators, in addition to possible legal action.

policy_description: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs
policydecision_details: Approved the National Policy for Critical and Strategic Minerals, classifying fertilisers as strategic inputs for food security. The proposal includes phosphates, potash and nitrogen fertilizers in mechanisms for tax incentives, credit, incentivized debentures and productive investment, aligned with the National Fertilizer Plan. According to the Agricultural Parliamentary Front, the measure aims to reduce Brazil’s dependence on imports, which account for more than 80% of national fertilizer consumption.
policycategory: Local production of fertilisers and other agricultural inputs

policycategory: Plant health measures|Water policies and regulations

The Maldives government and Bank of Maldives are tightening controls on how much foreign currency people can spend abroad. The pressure is coming from several directions at once: rising import bills, a tourism slowdown, and a debt repayment cycle that has drained reserves faster than they can be rebuilt.

The U.S. House has passed legislation that would allow nationwide year‑round sales of gasoline containing 15% ‌ethanol, handing a major win to biofuel producers and farm groups while raising concerns among refiners about higher compliance costs.
decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

policydecision_details: On 12 May 2026 GMT+7, the Cabinet approved in principle a draft royal decree amending the list of business types under the Foreign Business Act of 1999 as well as approving in principle a draft ministerial regulation specifying businesses that foreigners can operate without requiring permission.

Germany's cabinet approved the building modernisation act on 13 May, sending it to parliament for further deliberation, with only minor changes from the original draft. The new act will remove the existing requirement that new heating systems run on at least 65pc renewable energy. Instead, owners will again be able to choose between technologies, including gas and oil boilers, heat pumps, district heating, biomass installations or hybrid systems.

The European Investment Bank (EIB) has approved a €200 million loan to the Croatian Bank for Reconstruction and Development (HBOR) the loan will support investments by Croatian companies and public entities across the country.
Moldova has abandoned the practice of state regulation of prices for socially important goods, introduced in the pre-pandemic and pandemic period, Moldovan Minister of Economy Yevgeny Osmokescu said.

policycategory: Transport regulation and infrastructure|Financial support through public banks

policydecision_details: Announced a reduction in regulatory barriers for foreign investors following the Thai Cabinet’s approval in principle of proposed amendments to the Foreign Business Act, B.E. 2542 (1999) (the “FBA”). Thailand’s Cabinet approved in principle two legislative measures proposed by the Ministry of Commerce: i) a draft Royal Decree amending the categories of businesses listed under the FBA; ii) a draft Ministerial Regulation prescribing businesses that may be operated by foreign investors without obtaining approval under the FBA.

Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1124 temporarily suspends the EU customs inward processing regime for raw cane sugar used to produce white sugar. The Commission introduces this measure because the mechanism allowing duty-free processing and re-export of such sugar could distort the EU sugar market or contribute to market disruption. By suspending this special customs arrangement, imports of raw cane sugar for refining within the EU become subject to normal customs duties and rules, reducing arbitrage opportunities. The regulation is based on the Common Agricultural Policy framework and aims to stabilize the internal sugar market. It entered into force upon publication and applies until 27 May 2027.

Approved in principle draft measures to delist nine business activities from the Foreign Business Act (FBA) and ease licensing for foreign firms. The move aims to modernise regulations and boost competitiveness, while still requiring compliance with existing laws; the drafts are under review before taking effect.

Approved three strategic PPP projects to boost infrastructure base and stimulate economic growth across critical sectors. The approvals followed regulatory oversight by the Infrastructure Concession Regulatory Commission (ICRC). The projects include the development of a Smart National Transport Data Bank under the Nigerian Institute of Transport Technology , the Independent Power Projects (IPPs) at the Onne Port Complex and the Apapa Port Complex.

The STIP is being developed under the Climate Investment Funds Industry Decarbonisation Programme and is expected to be submitted to the CIF for review in October 2026.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Announced a regulation to determine which products will remain subject to the Industrialized Products Tax even after the country's tax overhaul takes effect. Brazil’s tax reform already established that the IPI would apply to products competing with goods manufactured in the Manaus Free Trade Zone that are produced elsewhere in Brazil or imported.
Türkiye unveils a new financial package worth USD 5.3 billion (TL 240.62 billion) to support transformation and employment in the agriculture sector in the country.

In adopting the 20th sanctions package on April 24, the EU banned the export to Kyrgyzstan of computer numerical control machines, which are used in the production of high-precision components for weaponry and telecommunications equipment crucial to drone operations.
Finland is planning to tighten restrictions on exports of medical equipment and healthcare technology to Russia.
The new legislation agreed on Tuesday seeks to foster the right to autonomy for adults across the EU.

Romania’s Senate approved legislation granting a series of tax incentives for companies in the domestic chemical industry using natural gas as feedstock, as authorities seek to encourage higher-value industrial processing of the country’s gas resources.

Prime Minister on Tuesday directed the authorities concerned to ensure the timely provision of fertiliser to farmers at all costs and ordered continuous monitoring of fertiliser supplies to safeguard the country’s food security.

Slovenia officially passed the Act on Intervention Measures for the Development of Slovenia (ZIURS ) on May 11, 2026. This comprehensive law introduces significant changes; 0 percent VAT on food, lower rental taxes, social cap, and even lower taxes for sole proprietors.

policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water|Transport regulation and infrastructure

policydecision_details: Announced a GYD 3 billion (USD 14.1 million) support package for rice farmers affected by rising fertiliser and fuel costs. The funds will be distributed as GYD 15 000 (USD 70) per acre for farmers with less than 50 acres of rice fields, and GYD 10 000 (USD 46) per acre for those with more than 50 acres.

decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

The Singapore Food Agency reaffirmed that selling expired food is illegal and is investigating the case, while urging retailers to ensure food safety and consumers to check expiry dates and report concerns.
Uzbekistan and the Philippines agreed to strengthen cooperation on competition policy and institutional capacity during the ICN 2026 conference, with plans for future joint initiatives.
Revoked the license of GLOBAL INSURANCE GROUP under national licensing laws. The company must still honor all existing insurance and reinsurance obligations.

The announcement reflects rising international interests in the country's frontier acreage and signals a renewed push to attract investment into high-potential offshore assets. The African Energy Chamber (AEC) welcomes the tender as a strong indication of growing investor confidence in Central Africa’s upstream sector. For the Chamber, the licensing round highlights São Tomé and Principe’s role in unlocking new hydrocarbon frontiers, strengthening regional energy integration and reinforcing Africa’s position as a competitive destination for exploration capital.
decision_making_institution: Government of São Tome and Principe

Aimed to unlock new growth by prioritizing administrative and business reforms, with the Prime Minister emphasizing that simplifying procedures is one of the fastest ways to boost economic activity and confidence.

Imposed a complete ban on import of plant-based food products originating from Nepal. The decision follows the detection of insects in recently imported Nepali goods such as fermented leafy greens, millet, soybean, maize and buckwheat.

Released a series of regulatory, administrative, and operational measures that collectively reinforce SAT’s transition toward predictive tax supervision, digital interoperability, and enhanced compliance monitoring.

Approved a plan to shift from a sector-specific response to a broader inter-ministerial strategy to protect cocoa industry, which has been hit by falling international prices, weak local processing capacity, logistical bottlenecks and smuggling. The measures under consideration therefore extend beyond short-term support. They include tax incentives for exporters using official trade channels and repatriating export revenues to the DRC, continued distribution of improved seeds and fermentation equipment, and the construction of warehouses and storage facilities. The government also plans to organize smallholder farmers into cooperatives to strengthen their bargaining power and reduce dependence on intermediaries.
decision_making_institution: Government of Democratic Republic of the Congo

policydecision_details: On May 8, 2026 it was published the final rule that updates retailer stocking standards in the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). This rule ensures that retailers carry a variety of foods that promote the health of SNAP participants. The rule also simplifies how foods are categorized, making the requirements easier for retailers to implement and FNS to oversee, strengthening the integrity of SNAP at all levels.

policydecision_details: Agreed to part of the demands made by the rural caucus and accepted the inclusion of some changes in the supplementary bill that cut fuel taxes in 2026. The proposal creates an exception to Brazil’s Fiscal Responsibility Law (LRF) by allowing revenue losses from fuel tax cuts to be offset through extraordinary federal revenue generated by oil price shocks, not through increases in other taxes, as current legislation requires. That includes additional royalty income, special participation payments, tax revenue from the oil and gas sector, proceeds from the sale of surplus pre-salt oil by PPSA and dividends paid to the federal government.

Australia will introduce a domestic gas reservation scheme from 1 July 2027, requiring exporters to supply 20% of gas to the local market to lower prices and support industry. Australian federal government statement, 07/05/2026.

Cell‑cultured foods are made by growing animal or plant cells in controlled environments to create alternatives to products like meat. In Australia and New Zealand, they have been regulated since June 2025 under Food Standards Australia New Zealand (FSANZ) standards covering safety, production, and mandatory labelling, and only approved products can be sold as minced meat, steak or chicken fillets.

Allocated about 13 billion drams (approximately USD 34 million) for road improvements. The program, presented by the Prime Minister, covers 57.5 km of highways, including 0.9 km of interstate, 26.7 km of national, and 29.9 km of regional roads, along with three transport facilities.

Morocco has moved to tighten controls on exports of copper alloy ingots, requiring prior authorization for overseas shipments under new rules aimed at safeguarding domestic supply and curbing market distortions.

Published an ordinance to formally establish the National Clinical Research Program, expected to reorganize and enhance clinical research in Brazil, making it more modern and nationally integrated.

Advanced a strategy to enhance the value chains of its special economic zones (SEZs). The government is accelerating SEZ development to attract investment in strategic sectors, including finance, high-quality tourism, and healthcare services.
