The legislation introduces a cap on the total repayment amount of consumer loans, limiting it to between 30%-50% above the amount borrowed-broadly in line with the European average.

Modified the regulatory framework for tobacco products, nicotine, and alternative consumption devices through a set of regulations covering foreign trade, health regulations, and administrative control. These measures are implemented through a decree from the National Executive Branch, a resolution from the Ministry of Health, and a provision from ANMAT (National Administration of Drugs, Food and Medical Technology), which together constitute different levels of decision-making within the Argentine legal system.

policy_description: Employment programmes|Agricultural expenditure in the national budget
policydecision_details: Approved a TZS 1.105 trillion (USD 409 million) for the Ministry of Agriculture for the 2026/27 financial year, paving the way for a nationwide rollout of the Bulding a Better Tomorrow programme. The initiative, targeting youth unemployment through commercial agriculture, is transitioning from pilot projects to full-scale implementation across councils and constituencies.
policycategory: Employment programmes|Agricultural expenditure in the national budget

policydecision_details: Promoted the formation of modern agricultural communities to shift from small-scale farming to more competitive, integrated agribusiness, supported by loans, a $35 million government credit package (2025–2027), and additional bank financing to boost productivity and scale. In addition, FTB Bank, Chip Mong Bank and Wing Bank have allocated around $25 million in financing for modern agricultural communities.
On May 4, Singapore and New Zealand signed the world’s first legally binding bilateral agreement to ensure that essential supplies will continue to flow smoothly, even in times of crisis.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Announced the authorisation for 5 000 MW of private renewable projects, bringing the total commitment for renewable capacity to 16 000 MW.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Announced that the daily minimum wage would increase up to USD 7.63.
Planned to phase out the CESS para-tariff by 2029 under a structured reform outlining timelines and safeguards to replace the long-standing levy. CESS: Commodity Export Subsidy Scheme.
Revealed an initiative to develop a regulatory framework to establish a minimum wage in the country.

Launched an emergency land reclamation project in May in the southern Gaza neighborhoods of al-Mughraqa, al-Sheikh Ajleen, and parts of al-Zaytoun in partnership with the Palestinian Agricultural Relief Society, the Agricultural Relief Society, the Cooperative Association for Grape and Vegetable Producers, and Oxfam.

Issued a notice implementing tariff-related elements of a memorandum of understanding concluded with Taiwan, province of China. This notice does not implement the terms of a subsequent bilateral agreement on reciprocal trade, which has not yet entered into force.

policy_description: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
policydecision_details: Announed the imposition of provisional anti-dumping duties on imports of light gauge steel studs and tracks originating from china.
policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures

policydecision_details: The Ministry of Labor, Family, Social Affairs and Equal Opportunities (MDDSZ) has officially extended the validity of the decree that allows for faster employment of foreigners. Originally set to expire on April 30, the accelerated procedures will now remain in effect until October 31, 2026.

policy_description: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations|Ecosystem and habitat preservation
policydecision_details: Implemented the annual fishing ban in the Gulf of Nicoya. This restriction period is vital for rigeneration of marine species and the overall health of the ecosystem.
policycategory: Fisheries and aquaculture measures and regulations|Ecosystem and habitat preservation

policy_description: Nutrition and health policy|Food safety regulations and standards
policydecision_details: Conducted a training to strengthen early warning surveillance systems and promote safer tourism practices.
policycategory: Nutrition and health policy|Food safety regulations and standards

policydecision_details: Enacted the provision 1/2026 joining Brazil and Uruguay in adopting regulatory frameworks that allow the issuance of a declaration directly by the exporter, gradually replacing - as will be seen later - the traditional Certificate of Origin managed before an authorized entity.

Raised diesel, kerosene and jet A-1 prices for the second consecutive month. The Energy Regulation Board (ERB) increased diesel prices from approximately USD 1.10 to USD 1.26 per liter, kerosene from USD 1.19 to USD 1.30 per liter, and Jet A-1 aviation fuel from USD 1.29 to USD 1.41 per liter. Petrol prices remained unchanged at approximately USD 1.01 per liter, as wholesale price movements stayed within the ERB's pricing adjustment threshold.

Announced that new minimum wage will take effect from January 2027, noting that the decision has taken into account the country's economic conditions, rising costs of living and the government's committment to boosting workers motivtion to enhance efficiency in services delivery.

Launched a pilot program that will provide free, easy-to-use chlorine water treatment to households through maternal and child health services, with the support of J-PAL Africa. By using routine health visits, similar to how other preventive health products like bed nets are given for free, the program aims to make safe drinking water reliable and accessible for households with young children.

Granted a one-month tax exemption on LNG imports to help reduce electricity costs. The measure, covering customs duty, commercial tax, and advance income tax, aims to lower power generation expenses amid rising global fuel prices.
Extended a six‑month ban on exports of ferrous scrap, effective May 1, covering waste and scrap from ferrous and non‑ferrous metals, including copper, aluminum, and lead.

Revised Fisheries Law introducing stricter aquaculture standards, limiting fishing capacity, and prohibiting unregistered vessels from operating or accessing fuel, water, or ice. The law was adopted on 27 Dec 2025.

The Guide to Canada’s Export Control List issued in January 2026, comes into effect from 1 May 2026, identifies the items included on the export control. Categories distinguish between U.S.-focused quotas (CUSMA) and EU-focused rules (CETA). In the agriculture and foods session, changes relate to milk products, peanut butter, sugar-contanig products and processed foods.

Proposed updates to its list of aquatic species susceptible to key diseases, seeking stakeholder input as part of efforts to strengthen import controls and domestic disease management for aquatic animals, given the significant risks such diseases pose to wild and farmed populations. This consultation ran from March 2, 2026, to May 1, 2027.

Enforced new regulations governing small commerce and retail trade. The reform reaffirms that small commerce and retail trade are reserved for Congolese economic operators. It maintains the government's position of protecting local commercial activities for nationals.The regulations also introduce an important distinction. Certain capital-intensive specialized retail activities will remain open to foreign investors, under conditions set by the regulations. The stated objective is not to exclude foreign capital entirely, but to redirect it toward segments requiring more structured investment.

Implemented the new EU Guidelines on preferential origin relating to the Interim Trade Agreement between EU and Mercosur. The preferential origin system introduced by the Agreement is based on self-certification by the exporter, replacing the traditional certificates issued by public authorities. The preferential tariff treatment must be requested by the importer and demonstrated through origin documentation; the request may also be made within two years from the date of importation. For EU exporters, the REX system is central: except for shipments of a value lower than EUR 6,000, registration and inclusion of the REX number in the origin attestations is required. For Mercosur countries, a five-year transitional regime is provided, allowing the use of certificates of origin issued by public authorities as an alternative to self-certifications. Other key provisions worth highlighting are: a general tolerance rule of 10% of the ex-works value for the use of non-originating materials; bilateral cumulation, under which originating materials from the EU used in processing in Mercosur may be treated as originating materials of Mercosur and vice versa; and the possibility of duty drawback, i.e. the refund or suspension of duties on non-originating materials used in the production of goods exported under preference.
Belarus raised export duties on liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) to the Russian level from May 1, 2026, with the corresponding resolution signed by Belarusian Prime Minister.
Continued to progressively expand general licenses for the energy sector activties involving Venezuelan-origin oil, gas and petrochemical activities.
Implemented zero-tariff treatment for imports from al 53 African countries with which it has diplomatic relations.

Issued new blocking sanctions on Cuba to operate in or have operated in the energy, defense and related materiels, metals and minim, financial services or security sector of the Cuban economy; be owned, controlled, or directed by, or to have acted or purported to act for on oh behalf of, directly or indirectly, the Government of Cuba; own or control, directly or indirectly, any person whose property or interests in property; have materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, the Government of Cuba or any person whose property or interests in property are blocked under this EO; be or have been a leader, official, senior executive officer, or member of the board of directors of the Government of Cuba or an entity whose property or interests in property are blocked under this EO; be a political subdivision, agency, or instrumentality of the Government of Cuba; be responsible for or complicit in, or to have directly or indirectly engaged in or attempted to engage in, serious human rights abuse in Cuba;be responsible for or complicit in, or to have directly or indirectly engaged or attempted to engage in, corruption related to Cuba, including corruption by, on behalf of, or otherwise related to the Government of Cuba, or a current or former official at any level of the Government of Cuba, such as the misappropriation of public assets, expropriation of private assets for personal gain or political purposes, or bribery; orbe an adult family member of a person designated under this EO.
decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

policydecision_details: Launched the Food Safety and Quality Authority's (FSQA) Strategic Plan for 2026-2030. This strategic plan outlines the Authority's vision, strategic priorities, and key interventions aimed at strengthening food safety and quality systems, enhancing regulatory effectiveness, and safeguarding public health in The Gambia over the medium term. The landmark event gathered key stakeholders from the government, development partners, and the private sector, highlighting the government's commitment to ensuring that citizens have broad access to quality and safe food.

Adopted a new law to reorganize the country's drinking water supply and sanitation sector. The reform is designed to improve access to clean water, strengthen hygiene systems, and attract private investment into a sector considered vital for public health and development.

Notified rice importers an updated framework that introduces an annual authorization process for customs clearence, tightening oversigth of the secto amid a broader push to strengthen domestic revenue collection and trade governance.
Outlined the 1 May Day worker protections, including a higher holiday bonus for gig workers (minimum 25% of average net income) and a nationwide minimum wage increase.

Accused China of circumventing import restrictions by routing vegetables through Vietnam and relabeling them as Vietnamese products. The claims come as Taiwan, Province of China maintains a ban on more than 1,000 Chinese agricultural and fishery items.
decision_making_institution: Government of Taiwan Province of China

policydecision_details: Signed a project with FAO funded by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) to establish a National Forest Monitoring and Assessment (NFMA) system. The project will introduce regular national forest inventories, combining field data with remote sensing and GIS to produce reliable information on forest cover, health, biodiversity, and carbon stocks.

Banned the import of goods made wholly or partly through forced labour under a new Commerce Ministry order. Importers will have to provide documentary proof that their products are free from forced labour.

Announced the mandatory ethanol blend in gasoline from 30 to 32 percent and increased the biodiesel mandate from 15 to 16 percent. This increase will require that more maize output will shift from feed industry to fuel industry.
The Korea Credit Guarantee Fund (KODIT) and Woori Bank signed an agreement enabling KODIT to provide KRW 222 billion (USD 150 million)in loan guarantees to support SMEs affected by the global crisis.

Announced minimum wage adjustments for the years 2026 and 2027. Adjustments vary from 60 percent to 70 percent and the wage difference for the months prior to the measure (from January to April 2026) must be compensated by companies by 31 July 2026.
Introduced a 18 percent VAT obligations on B2C sales for non-resident suppliers of digital services and online goods (Minsterial Order No 004/26/10/TC).

Established, with the Administrative Resolution No 0009/2026 of the National Health Authority of Nicaragua, the full digitalization of procedures for products intended for human consumption and definitively eliminating the use of paper in the registration and renewable processes for food and beverages. The new regulation requires that all applications be processed exclusively through the Karplus System. This platform now centralizes all procedures related to new sanitary registrations, renewals (with or without changes), and modifications.

The State Bank of Vietnam is drafting a new circular to revise foreign exchange management regulations for foreign direct investment into Vietnam, allowing earlier opening of investment accounts and improving flexibility in capital flow management. The draft circular is intended to replace Circular 06/2019/TT-NHNN.

Introduced hourly wage model and equal pay reforms as part of broader labour reforms. The minimum wage has risen to 345 manats (about USD 203), the average monthly salary to 1,099 manats (about USD 646), and the minimum pension to 320 manats (about USD 188).

Ruled out a 25% tax on existing gas export contracts, rejecting what was described as a “populist” proposal. Emphasizing that a global fuel crisis is the worst time to risk relations, the decision aims to protect partnerships with Asian trading partners, and the upcoming federal budget will not include such a tax.

Urged national consensus to shift from crisis response to long-term water security, including building large reservoirs and dams, stressing that Pakistan’s water challenges cannot be addressed in isolation.
The Central Bank of Uzbekistan has amended foreign exchange rules, allowing individuals to transfer funds for personal, non‑commercial purposes between any bank accounts.
Announced that USD 1 billion from the National Development Fund will be allocated to import basic goods such as sugar, rice, red meat and animal feed.

policy_description: Subsidies on fuel, power and water
policydecision_details: Decided to implement some cuts in public spending to make funds available to offer independent bus operators of the Belize Bus Association a USD 3.00 per gallon fuel subisidy.
policycategory: Subsidies on fuel, power and water

policydecision_details: Issued a new decree to revise the classified list of tree species for log exports. The number of tree species banned from log exports has been increased to 91, with only 23 species remaining approved for export. Additionally, an additional export tax on unprocessed forest products will be levied on these permitted species.
Adopted the National Policy on Food and Nutrition 2026-2035 and directed the Federal Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning to present the policy to the Federal Executive Council for ratification.

policy_description: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures
policydecision_details: Launched a public–private Voluntary Carbon Market Alliance, chaired by the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry, to serve as a governance platform linking supply and demand, addressing regulatory gaps, and supporting market activity.
policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Reviewed a draft law since March 18, 2026 to amend the Customs Code, aiming to comprehensively regulate e‑commerce within national and EAEU customs frameworks by introducing new provisions to the existing legislation, the Code of Kazakhstan "On Customs Regulation in the Republic Of Kazakhstan".

FAO will deliver cash assistance directly to beneficiaries via bKash, improving transparency, security, and efficiency. Recipients can instantly access funds in their accounts and use them for everyday needs such as payments, transfers, and mobile services without visiting agents.

Planned to introduce a five-year income tax exemption for new immigrants and returning residents relocating in 2026, covering locally earned income such as salaries and self-employment earnings, as part of efforts to encourage aliyah.

The World Bank has endorsed USD 24.5mn in grant financing for the Technical Assistance for Sustainable Agricultural Transformation (TASAT) project in Philippines. The funding acts as a companion to a massive USD 1bn loan intended to pivot the country away from its rigid obsession with rice self-sufficiency.

policy_description: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures
policydecision_details: Confirmed the continuation of anti-dumping duties on imported acrylic sheets from China following the first sunset review. This decision affects directly manufacturers and integrators of cold storage systems.
policycategory: Anti-dumping duties, countervailing duties, safeguard measures

policydecision_details: Approved the Judges Salaries and Pensions Bill 2025 to fulfil a constitutional obligation and correct a gap in which judges, unlike magistrates, do not receive pension. The pension will be calculated solely on the basis of salary, not alowances.

Implemented the Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Bill 2025, by issuing a Logitech webcam and USB hub adapter to each senator to promote uniformity, reliability and the overall quality of virtual sittings and to strengthen the official record of proceedings. The Act does not apply to any owner or occupier of a private residence, the surrounding land, or any associated property where a domestic worker provides domestic work.

The government plans to reform land administration by reclaiming unused and illegally occupied public land, introducing digital systems, streamlining registration processes, and strengthening oversight to improve transparency, reduce corruption, and protect agricultural land.

policy_description: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection
policydecision_details: Proposed new e‑commerce rules to strengthen consumer protection, addressing complaints on product quality, payments, and delivery. About 60% of cases were resolved in favor of consumers, with compensation totaling roughly 350 million soums (around USD 28,000).
policycategory: Legal and regulatory measures for consumer protection

policydecision_details: Launched the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy in Accra. The strategy addresses sectors including healthcare, agriculture, education, finance, and public service delivery, and covers measures including AI training for government ministers, the introduction of AI performance indicators across ministries, departments and agencies, and the deployment of AI by the Ghana Revenue Authority. The government states that the strategy aims to position Ghana as an AI hub in West Africa and to localise AI systems to reflect Ghanaian languages and cultural contexts. Implementation will be coordinated across government institutions including the National Information Technology Agency, Data Protection Commission, and Cyber Security Authority, with support from international partners including GIZ, UNDP, and UNESCO.
Introduced new import tariffs ranging from 5 percent to 35 percent on 185 HS codes, covering finished goods and industrial outputs.

Implemented new import licensing rules for rice effectively halting shipments to Cotonou port and triggering a price slide in Indian markets. Importers must hold a USD 1.7 million deposit in a Public Treasury account and commit to monthly volumes of 50 000-100 000 tonnes.

The Republic is buying additional liquefied natural gas (LNG) from other parts of the world as the conflict in the Middle East disrupts shipments of the commodity used to generate electricity in the country.

Increased the maximum retail price of petro to RWF 2 938 (USD 0.88) per litre, while capping diesel at RWF 2 205 (USD 1.51) per litre, with the government intervening to shild transport and logistics from sharper costs increases.

The government decided on Tuesday, April 14th, that a solidarity levy will be imposed on fuel retailers if their actual retail price exceeds the objectively calculated price by more than 3%. The final decision on the draft law prepared by the Ministry of Economics (EM) will be made by the Saeima.

policy_description: Public institution|Establishment or modification of food stock
policydecision_details: Gazzetted the Food Reserve Act 2026, to continue the existence of the Food Reserve Agency and re-define its functions; re constitute the Board of the Agency and re-define its functions, continue the existence of the National Strategic Food Reserve; ensure national food security by maintaining sufficient levels of designated agricultural commodities to respond and provide food relief during emergencies or market and economic shocks; provide for the power of the Minister to designate agricultural commodities that are essential for food security; provide for the purchase of designated agricultural commodities by the Agency for purposes of the National Strategic Food Reserve; provide mechanisms for collaboration and cooperation with relevant regulatory and advisory agencies to ensure exchange of agricultural marketing information and the stabilisation of agricultural markets; repeal and replace the Food Reserve Act, 2020; and provide for matters connected with, or incidental to, the foregoing.

policycategory: Climate change mitigation and adaptation measures

policydecision_details: Provided to nearly 200 women rice processors to boost their equipment. The beneficiaries are organised into five cooperatives across the Central, Kara and Savanes regions, have recently received modern rice parboiling kits as part of the West African Food System Resilience Programme (FSRP). This equipment includes soaking tanks with capacities ranging from 800 kg to one tonne, 120-kg parboiling machines fitted with stainless steel sieves and fuelled by improved stoves, as well as drying tarpaulins. This material support is complemented by technical and entrepreneurial training designed to strengthen management capacities and improve the profitability of the activities.

Announces the approval of the licence for Credit & Data Bureau Solomon Islands Limited (CDBSIL), to operate as a Credit Reporting Service Provider in Solomon Islands, in accordance with the Solomon Islands Credit Reporting Regulations 2025.

Enacted a new 16 percent consumption tax applied to online games of chance operated exclusively over internet with no VAT credit available on operating costs. A complementary tax normalization at a 19% rate is reintroduced for omitted assets or elimination of nonexistent liabilities as of 1 April 2026, with filing and payment due by 31 July 2026.
Amended the sections 1020.02; 2022.01; 2022.02; 6020.03 and 6020.10of the Incentive Code (2019).

policydecision_details: Introduced 100 percent discount on iFood Club monthly fee for teachers, a subscription model that gather advantages within the platform conditioning access to the automatic validation of the CNBD in the offical system of the federal government.

Enacted the revised Foreign Trade Law of the People’s Republic of China, adopted on December 27, 2025. The updated legislation marks a notable shift in China’s trade policy, moving beyond its previous emphasis on openness to international trade toward a framework that places greater weight on protecting the domestic economy. This change is reflected in Article 1 of the law, which explicitly highlights objectives such as safeguarding national sovereignty, security, and development interests.

Successfully delivered the country’s first-ever climate risk parametric insurance payouts, under its regulatory sandbox, following the heavy rainfall event of January 2026. The payouts, issued under the innovative TrigaCash insurance product represent a major advancement in efforts to build climate and financial resilience for vulnerable households across the nation. TrigaCash is the Solomon Islands’ first-ever climate-risk parametric microinsurance product, a unique safety net that pays out automatically based on verified weather data without the usual claims hassle. It protects farmers, fishers, small business owners and families against heavy rainfall, cyclonic winds and drought, helping communities bounce back faster from climate shocks.

Announced an agreement with Malaysia to avoid double taxation. It enhances tax certainty, reduces the risk of double taxation, and supports the expansion of cross-border trade, investment, and business activities between the two jurisdictions. Businesses and investors with interests in either jurisdiction are encouraged to assess the potential impact of the treaty on their existing and future structures, transactions, and overall tax positions.

Launched a new 2026-2027 investment strategy focused on infrastructure, energy, human capital and private sector competitiveness, to strengthen the impact of public investments. Flagship projects include the Tambacounda dry port, the Grand Water Transfer project, the Southern and Central agropoles, and the ports of Ndayane and Sendou. For the 2026 fiscal year, the government allocated CFA2 384.3 billion (USD 4 billion) to public investment.

Signed the Water Supply Project with EU. The Water Supply Project in the Greater Banjul Area (WASIB) will finance critical infrastructure to provide safely managed drinking water services in the Greater Banjul Area, The Gambia. WASIB addresses several challenges in the area, including ageing water supply facilities, high levels of non-revenue water, intermittent water supply, and depleting groundwater resources. The project covers both drilling and emergency works necessary to maintain and improve service continuity for about 560,000 people (approximately 25% of the country's population). It also includes water production and treatment, as well as water transmission, storage, and distribution for approximately 300,000 additional new beneficiaries.

Received the approval for a USD 45 million grant from the World Bank in financing the IDA to support the government's effort to enhance domestic revenue mobilization, lay key infrastructure, regulatory skill foundations for private sector development, and strengthen climate resilience.
Sanctioned a network of front companies and shipping facilitators that bankroll the Iranian armed forces by selling crude oil.
decision_making_institution: Government of United States of America

policydecision_details: Decided to postpone until further notice the export period of shea kernels for the 2025-2026 campaign.

Signed three agreements in the telecommunication sector. These committments aim to improve connectivity, facilitate cross-border communications and consolidate the digital ecosystem in Central Africa. The first agreement concerns the coordination of frequencies at the borders; the second agreement introduces the free roaming between Gabon and Equatorial Guinea; the third agreement concerns interconnection via the CAB-4 fibre optic cable.

Announced an ambitious plan to constructu an additional 700 km of roads across the country. The initiative is aimed at improving connectivity nationwide and addressing the longstanding challenges posed by poor road conditions that many communities have endured for decades.
Launched the Gender Equality Seal for Public Institutions to support public instititions to ensure that gender equality is fully integrated into the core of public service delivery.
Enforced strict biosecurity protocols, including restricting animal movement, isolating infected cattle from healthy ones, and disinfecting affected areas.

Officials added that the decree supports Axis 3 of President Abdourahamane Tchiani’s development plan, which focuses on building production capacity and advancing economic self-reliance through the promotion of local industries.
policycategory: Government procurement from domestic farmers|Government procurement through imports

Adopted a draft decree on the increase of the guaranteed interprofessional minimum wage (SMIG) which goes from CFA 30 047 (USD 43) to CFA 42 000 (USD 74). This measure directly responds to the demand of the social partners.
Decided to renew the ban on the export of cereals.

Approved in the Council of Ministers a decree establishing the National Centre for the Improvement of Animal Production. According to the authorities, this new entity will be mandated to develop a national policy for the improvement of local breeds through appropriate methods, in order to increase the milk and meat production performance of local breeds. The government plans to strengthen the capacities of local livestock farms in order to substitute imports of milk and milk products.

policy_description: Financial support through public banks|Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: Received the approval of a new refinancing line from the West African Development Bank to finance SMEs and solar energy.
policycategory: Financial support through public banks|Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: Created the national observatory on work and professional training. A strategic tool for monitoring the labour market The ONEF was created in the form of a Public Administrative Establishment (EPA). Its establishment aims to provide Niger with a modern instrument for monitoring, analysing and planning employment and training. Its main missions will be to monitor the evolution of the labour market and its labor needs.

Provided 324 women with goat kits consisting of three animal per women: one male breeding and two female breeding goats. The aim of this initiative is to support women's efforts to strengthen food security and the resilience of vulnerable households by supporting their productive livestock capital to enable them to cope with climatic and economic crises.
Approved an action plan for the resuming works on irrigated perimeter of public area of Kessa (110 hectares)

Received a USD 30.25 million financing support from African Development Bank for a climate protection and agriculture sector resilience program in the northern part of the country. his initiative will protect 150,000 smallholder farmers against climate shocks in a country where agriculture employs seven out of ten people but remains at the mercy of an increasingly unpredictable climate. The situation is particularly critical in the departments of Alibori and Atakora, where one in four farmers suffers from food insecurity, well above the national average.

Sigend a Free Trade Agreement with UK, including provisions to enhace intellectual property protection by streamlining procedures, reducing administrative burdens and speeding up processes to ensure transparency and legal certainty.

Issued Decision No. 20/2025/QD-TTg, to delineate the catalogue of important data and core data. Effective immediately, it specifies classification and management protocols for data, including core data such as national border data, defence and national security strategies, public health statistics, economic policies, and environmental data. It also covers important data related to sectors such as transportation, finance, agriculture, and public administration.

policy_description: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures
policydecision_details: The European Commission has approved a EUR 3.7 billion (USD 4.2 billion) Czech scheme to support the construction of biomethane production stations in line with the objectives of the Clean Industrial Deal. This measure will contribute to the transition towards a net-zero economy. The scheme was approved under the Clean Industrial Deal State Aid Framework (CISAF) adopted by the Commission on 25 June 2025.
policycategory: Renewable energy and energy efficiency measures

policydecision_details: EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic emphasized the EU's priority for a fair agreement over unjustified tariffs, after the meeting with US officials in Washington ended. The US announced 25 percent tariffs on countries buying Venezuelan oil.

Launched a framework to improve the speed and effectiveness of outbreak detection and response. The goal is to detect the disease pathogen within seven days, notify within one day, and launch an effective response within seven days.

country: Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)

Published the Food Act 2022, prescripting that: i) no person shall import to into Mauritius any unsafe, misbranded or sub-standard food; ii) no person shall import to Mauritius any article of food which does not comply with the act.
Enacted the Food Safety Act, providing a strong foundation for aligning the Maldives' food safety system with international standards.

policy_description: Unspecified agricultural tax|Tax on inputs or fixed capital
policydecision_details: On March 20, 2024, the Ministry of Economy and Finance issued Prakas No.170 on Tax Incentives for the Agricultural Sector. This regulation aims to consolidate previous tax incentives into a single document and expands the scope of agricultural products eligible for these incentives. The tax incentives apply to the planting, producing, local supplying, and exporting of paddy rice, rice, corn, beans, peppers, cassava, cashew nuts, rubber, Pailin longans, mangos, bananas, as well as livestock farming, aquacultures, and local oil palm products used as raw materials for producing animal feed. Enterprises operating within the scope of this Prakas are eligible for a range of tax incentives, including: 1. Suspension of the monthly prepayment of income tax and the minimum tax until the end of 2025. 2. Exemption from the withholding obligation on payments for services performed by persons not under the self-assessment regime until the end of 2025. 3. The value-added tax will be borne by the State. To qualify for these tax incentives, enterprises in the agricultural sector must comply with key conditions outlined in this Prakas, such as keeping proper accounting records and filing tax returns correctly, among others. Non-compliance with these requirements could lead to the revocation of the tax incentives.
decision_making_institution: the Ministry of Economy and Finance

policydecision_details: Authorised the re-export petroleum operations to allow foreign traders to import fule, store it temporarily in Gambian tanks, and then re-export it to neighbouring countries. The goal was to boost storage use, earn handling fees, and create a West African fuel hub.

Negotiators from the EU and the East African Community (EAC- which comprises Burundi, Kenya, Rwanda, Tanzania and Uganda) finalised a new comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (EPA) between both regions. The EPA eliminates customs duties and covers other important issues, such as free movement of goods, cooperation on customs and taxation, and trade defense instruments, which mirror the effort of the EAC to strengthen its customs union and to set up an effective internal market. The agreement, initialized today by all negotiators, is now going to be presented for approval according to the domestic procedures of each partner.
contextoradditionalinfo: In 2007, the East African Community finalised a framework agreement on tariff elimination, which became a basis for the comprehensive EPA, initialized today. In 2013, total trade between the EU and the EAC amounted to €5.8 billion. The EU imports from the EAC are worth €2.2 billion and consist mostly of coffee, cut flowers, tea, tobacco, fish and vegetables. Exports from the EU into the EAC, mainly machinery and mechanical appliances, equipment and parts, vehicles and pharmaceutical products, amount to €3.5 billion.

policy_description: Opinions of the General Office of the State Council on Adopting an All-Encompassing Approach to Food and Building a Diversified Food Supply System
policydecision_details: The Opinions of the General Office of the State Council on Adopting an All-Encompassing Approach to Food and Building a Diversified Food Supply System is a strategic guidance policy document proposed by the Chinese government to cope with future food security and sustainable development challenges and strengthen food supply security. The Opinions mainly focus on the big food view and aim to broaden food sources and build a diversified food supply system to ensure China's food security and nutritional needs. The core concept of the Big Food View is to break through the traditional thinking of single supply of grains such as rice, wheat, and corn, and extensively develop and utilize various food resources, including grains, grains, feed, vegetables, fruits, fish, livestock, bacteria, insects, and other resources, forming a diversified food supply system. This comprehensive and multi-channel food security concept not only focuses on the food on arable land, but also involves the development and utilization of non-traditional food resources such as aquatic products, agroforestry, forage, grassland resources, and microorganisms. Key points proposed in the document include: 1.Diversified Agricultural Production: Promoting other crops like beans, potatoes, and developing livestock, fishery, and modern agriculture technologies; 2. Technological Innovation: Encouraging innovations in agriculture (e.g., gene breeding, smart agriculture) to boost production efficiency; 3. Sustainable Resource Use: Enhancing land and water use efficiency through practices like water-saving agriculture; 4. Green and Circular Agriculture: Reducing the environmental impact by promoting sustainable and low-carbon farming; International Cooperation on Food Security: Strengthening global agricultural partnerships and improving food reserves; Healthy Diets: Promoting balanced nutrition and food safety for better public health.

policy_description: Strategy on Aquaculture, Rural Development and Fishery 2017-2027
policydecision_details: The Strategy on Agriculture, Rural Development and Fisheries is a national policy with a cross-sectoral approach. The timeframe of the policy is 7 years between 2021 and 2027. The purposes of this policy are (I) to ensure the sustainable development of the agri-food sector to meet the needs of people facing medium and long-term challenges related to food security, livelihoods, climate change, and biodiversity loss, and (II) to develop rural households and become more competitive in rural areas, based on policies that support sustainable use of natural resources, efficient use of agricultural and fishing inputs, and agricultural knowledge and innovation.
